sentences.zh: 世家二○西蜀孟氏

translations.literal: Hereditary Houses 2 ○ The Meng Clan of Western Shu
translations.idiomatic: Hereditary Houses 2 — The Meng Clan of Western Shu

sentences.zh: 西蜀孟昶，初名仁讚，及僭位改焉。

translations.literal: Meng Chang of Western Shu; his original name was Renzan; when he assumed the imperial title he changed it.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Chang of Western Shu was originally named Renzan; he adopted the present name when he took the throne.

sentences.zh: 其先邢州龍岡人。

translations.literal: His ancestors were people of Longgang in Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His family came from Longgang in Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父知祥，事後唐武皇，武皇以弟之子妻之，是為瓊華長公主。

translations.literal: His father Zhixiang served Later Tang's Emperor Wu; the emperor gave him in marriage a daughter of his younger brother's line, who became Princess Qionghua the Elder.
translations.idiomatic: His father Meng Zhixiang served Emperor Wu of Later Tang, who gave him a bride from his younger brother's household; she became Princess Qionghua the Elder.

sentences.zh: 同光初，知祥為太原尹、知留守事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tongguang era, Zhixiang was mayor of Taiyuan and acting regent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tongguang reign, Zhixiang served as mayor of Taiyuan and acting regent of the capital.

sentences.zh: 三年，平蜀。

translations.literal: Year third, Shu was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Shu was pacified.

sentences.zh: 四年，以知祥為劍南西川節度副大使、知節度事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Zhixiang was appointed deputy military commissioner of Jiannan West Circuit and acting military governor.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was made deputy military commissioner of Jiannan West Circuit with authority over military affairs.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，命知祥討平東川，知祥自領兩川節度，明宗即以授之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, he ordered Zhixiang to pacify East River Circuit; Zhixiang then held both circuits himself, and Mingzong confirmed the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Mingzong came to the throne, he ordered Zhixiang to subdue East River Circuit; Zhixiang then took command of both river circuits, and the emperor ratified the arrangement.

sentences.zh: 長興四年，封蜀王，許行墨製。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Changxing, he was enfeoffed as King of Shu and permitted to issue orders in his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Changxing he was created King of Shu and allowed to issue edicts under his own seal.

sentences.zh: 五年，閔帝立，乃稱帝於蜀，改元明德，時清泰元年也。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when Emperor Min was enthroned, he declared himself emperor in Shu and changed the era name to Mingde—it was then the first year of Qingtai.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, after Emperor Min acceded, he declared himself emperor in Shu and adopted the era name Mingde, which corresponded to the first year of Qingtai.

sentences.zh: 事具《五代史》。

translations.literal: The matter is fully set forth in the History of the Five Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: The full account is given in the History of the Five Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 昶母李氏，本莊宗嬪禦，以賜知祥，天祐十六年己卯十一月，生昶於太原。

translations.literal: Chang's mother, the Lady Li, had originally been a consort of Emperor Zhuangzong and was given to Zhixiang; in the eleventh month of the jimao year, the sixteenth year of Tianyou, Chang was born at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's mother, Lady Li, had been a consort of Emperor Zhuangzong before she was given to Zhixiang; Chang was born at Taiyuan in the eleventh month of 919.

sentences.zh: 初，知祥鎮西川，不及以族行。

translations.literal: At first, when Zhixiang governed West River Circuit, he had not been able to bring his clan with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhixiang first took up his post in West River Circuit, he had been unable to move his family west with him.

sentences.zh: 天成元年，奏遣衙校迎家太原，明宗因令部送長公主及昶與所生母至蜀。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancheng he memorialized to send a staff officer to bring his household from Taiyuan; Mingzong then ordered an escort to convey the Elder Princess, Chang, and his birth mother to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiancheng he petitioned to send a staff officer to fetch his household from Taiyuan; Emperor Mingzong then had the Elder Princess, Chang, and his birth mother escorted to Shu.

sentences.zh: 公主以長興三年卒。

translations.literal: The Princess, in the third year of Changxing.
translations.idiomatic: The princess died in the third year of Changxing.

sentences.zh: 知祥初署昶西川節度行軍司馬，僭號，以昶為檢校太保、同平章事、崇聖宮使、東川節度。

translations.literal: Zhixiang first appointed Chang acting marshal on campaign for the West River military commission; when he assumed the imperial title, he made Chang honorary grand guardian, co-equal councilor, commissioner of the Chong Sheng Palace, and military governor of East River Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang first named Chang acting campaign marshal of the West River commission; when he took the throne he made Chang honorary grand guardian, chief councilor, commissioner of the Chong Sheng Palace, and military governor of East River Circuit.

sentences.zh: 知祥疾，立為皇太子，權監軍國。

translations.literal: When Zhixiang fell ill, he was installed as crown prince with authority to oversee state and military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhixiang fell ill, Chang was named crown prince and given charge of state and military affairs.

sentences.zh: 明德元年七月，知祥卒，昶襲位，年始十六，止稱明德年號，委政於趙季良、張知業、李仁罕等。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Mingde, Zhixiang died; Chang succeeded him at the age of only sixteen, kept only the Mingde era name, and entrusted government to Zhao Jiliang, Zhang Zhiye, Li Renhan, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of Mingde, Zhixiang died and Chang succeeded him at sixteen; he retained only the Mingde era name and left government to Zhao Jiliang, Zhang Zhiye, Li Renhan, and others.

sentences.zh: 二年，尊其母李氏為皇太后。

translations.literal: In the second year, he honored his mother, the Lady Li, as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he honored his mother, Lady Li, as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 四年，改元廣政。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he changed the era name to Guangzheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he changed the era name to Guangzheng.

sentences.zh: 後以事誅仁罕、知業，乃親政事。

translations.literal: Later, on account of certain matters, he executed Renhan and Zhiye and then took charge of government himself.
translations.idiomatic: Later he had Renhan and Zhiye executed over a political dispute and then took government into his own hands.

sentences.zh: 十三年，加號睿文英武仁聖明孝皇帝。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he added the title Emperor Ruiwen Yingwu Rensheng Mingxiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he took the fuller title Emperor Ruiwen Yingwu Rensheng Mingxiao.

sentences.zh: 晉末，秦州節度使何建、鳳州防禦使石奉頵俱以城降昶。

translations.literal: Late in Jin, Qinzhou military commissioner He Jian and Fengzhou defense commissioner Shi Fengyun both surrendered their cities to Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Jin period, Qinzhou military commissioner He Jian and Fengzhou defense commissioner Shi Fengyun both surrendered their cities to Chang.

sentences.zh: 時契丹亂華，漢祖起並門，中土蝗旱連歲，昶益自大，開貢部，行郊祀禮，自此君臣奢縱。

translations.literal: At that time the Khitans were ravaging China, the Han founder rose at Bingmen, and the central plain suffered locusts and drought year after year; Chang grew ever more arrogant, opened a tribute office, and performed suburban sacrifices—from then on ruler and ministers indulged in extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitans were then ravaging the north, the founder of Han rose at Taiyuan, and the heartland suffered locusts and drought for years on end; Chang grew ever bolder, opened a tribute office, and performed suburban sacrifices, and from that time court and ministers gave themselves over to luxury.

sentences.zh: 及周世宗克秦、鳳，昶始懼，放還先所獲濮州刺史胡立，致書世宗，稱大蜀皇帝，且言家世邢台，願敦鄉里之分。

translations.literal: When Later Zhou's Shizong took Qin and Feng, Chang first grew afraid; he released the Pu prefect Hu Li, whom he had earlier captured, and wrote to Shizong styling himself Emperor of Great Shu, saying that his family came from Xingtai and asking to renew ties as fellow townsfolk.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong of Later Zhou took Qin and Feng, Chang at last grew afraid; he released the Pu prefect Hu Li, whom he had earlier captured, and wrote to Shizong as Emperor of Great Shu, saying his family came from Xingtai and asking to renew their ties as fellow townsfolk.

sentences.zh: 世宗怒其無禮，不答。

translations.literal: Shizong was angered by his discourtesy and made no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong was angered by the discourtesy and made no reply.

sentences.zh: 昶愈不自安，乃於劍門、夔、峽多積芻粟，增置師旅。

translations.literal: Chang grew still more uneasy and therefore stockpiled fodder and grain at Jianmen, Kui, and Xia, and increased his armies.
translations.idiomatic: Chang grew still more uneasy and stockpiled fodder and grain at Jianmen, Kui, and Xia while expanding his armies.

sentences.zh: 用度不足，遂鑄鐵錢。

translations.literal: Revenue was insufficient, so he cast iron coin.
translations.idiomatic: When revenue fell short, he began casting iron coin.

sentences.zh: 禁境內鐵，凡器用須鐵為之者，置場鬻之，以專其利。

translations.literal: He banned iron within his borders; whatever utensils required iron were sold only at government depots, so that he might monopolize the profit.
translations.idiomatic: He banned private iron within his borders and required all iron goods to be sold at government depots, monopolizing the profit for himself.

sentences.zh: 立其子玄喆為太子，用王昭遠、伊審征、韓保正、趙崇韜等分掌機要，總內外兵柄。

translations.literal: He installed his son Xuanzhe as crown prince and employed Wang Zhaoyuan, Yi Shenzheng, Han Baozheng, Zhao Chongtao, and others to divide control of state secrets and to hold overall civil and military authority.
translations.idiomatic: He named his son Xuanzhe crown prince and put Wang Zhaoyuan, Yi Shenzheng, Han Baozheng, Zhao Chongtao, and others in charge of state affairs and all military power, civil and military alike.

sentences.zh: 母李氏謂昶曰：“吾嚐見莊宗跨河與梁軍戰，又見爾父在并州捍契丹及入蜀定兩川，當時主兵者非有功不授，故士卒畏服。

translations.literal: His mother, the Lady Li, said to Chang: "I once saw Emperor Zhuangzong cross the river to fight the Liang armies, and I also saw your father at Bingzhou repel the Khitans and enter Shu to settle the two circuits; in those days commanders were appointed only for merit, so the soldiers feared and obeyed them.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Li, told Chang: "I once saw Emperor Zhuangzong cross the Yellow River to fight the Liang armies, and I saw your father at Taiyuan hold off the Khitans and then enter Shu to secure both river circuits; in those days only men with real merit received command, and the troops obeyed them out of respect.

sentences.zh: 如昭遠者，出於微賤，但自爾就學之年，給事左右；

translations.literal: Men like Zhaoyuan rose from humble origins and have served only at your side since the years when you first went to school;
translations.idiomatic: Men like Zhaoyuan came up from nothing and have done nothing but wait on you since you were a schoolboy;

sentences.zh: 又保正等皆世祿之子，素不知兵，一旦邊疆警急，此輩有何智略以禦敵？

translations.literal: and Baozheng and the rest are sons of hereditary stipend holders who have never known war—if the frontier suddenly alarms, what strategy have such men to meet the enemy?"
translations.idiomatic: and Baozheng and the rest are sons of court families who have never known war—if the frontier suddenly catches fire, what strategy do such men have to meet the enemy?"

sentences.zh: 高彥儔是爾父故人，秉心忠實，多所經練，此可委任。”

translations.literal: Gao Yanchou is an old companion of your father's, loyal at heart and widely experienced—he is the man to entrust."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yanchou is an old companion of your father's, loyal at heart and seasoned in affairs—he is the man you should trust.

sentences.zh: 昶不能遵用其言。

translations.literal: Chang could not follow her advice.
translations.idiomatic: Chang could not bring himself to follow her advice.

sentences.zh: 及太祖下荊、楚，昶欲遣使朝貢，昭遠等固止之。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor conquered Jing and Chu, Chang wished to send envoys with tribute, but Zhaoyuan and the others firmly dissuaded him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor conquered Jing and Chu, Chang wished to send tribute envoys, but Zhaoyuan and the others firmly dissuaded him.

sentences.zh: 太祖詔蜀之邸吏、將卒先在江陵者並放還，仍給賜錢帛以遣。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor ordered that all lodge clerks and officers and soldiers of Shu then at Jiangling be released and sent home, and gave them money and silks for the journey.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor ordered all Shu lodge clerks and troops then at Jiangling released and sent home with gifts of money and silk.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年，昶遣孫遇、楊蠲、趙彥韜為諜至京師。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiande, Chang sent Sun Yu, Yang Juan, and Zhao Yantao as spies to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qiande, Chang sent Sun Yu, Yang Juan, and Zhao Yantao to the capital as spies.

sentences.zh: 彥韜潛取昶與并州劉鈞蠟丸帛書以告，其書云：“早歲曾奉尺書，遠達睿聽。

translations.literal: Yantao secretly took a wax-sealed letter on silk from Chang to Liu Jun of Bingzhou and reported it; the letter read: "In earlier years I once sent a letter that reached your sage hearing from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Yantao secretly seized a wax-sealed letter on silk from Chang to Liu Jun of Bingzhou and turned it in; it read: "In earlier years I once sent a letter that reached your sage hearing from afar.

sentences.zh: 丹素備陳於翰墨，歡盟已保於金蘭。

translations.literal: Loyal intent was fully prepared in writing, and the alliance of friendship was secured as gold and orchid.
translations.idiomatic: My loyal intent was fully set forth in writing, and our bond of friendship was secured like gold and orchid.

sentences.zh: 洎傳吊伐之嘉音，實動輔車之喜色。

translations.literal: When the good news of punitive expedition was transmitted of punitive expedition, it truly moved the joy of chariot-ally states.
translations.idiomatic: When word came of the gracious tidings of punitive expedition, it truly stirred the joy of allied states.

sentences.zh: 尋於褒、漢，添駐師徒，隻待靈旗之濟河，便遣前鋒而出境。”

translations.literal: Soon afterward at Bao and Han I added stationed troops, waiting only for the sacred banners to cross the river before sending the vanguard beyond the border."
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward I added troops at Bao and Han, waiting only for the sacred banners to cross the river before sending the vanguard beyond the border."

sentences.zh: 先是，太祖已有西伐意而未發，及覽書，喜曰：“吾用師有名矣。”

translations.literal: Earlier the Founding Emperor had already intended a western campaign but had not yet launched it; when he read the letter he said with pleasure: "Now I have a righteous name for taking up arms."
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor had already intended a western campaign but had not yet launched it; when he read the letter he said with pleasure: "Now I have a righteous name for taking up arms."

sentences.zh: 即命忠武軍節度王全斌充鳳州路行營前軍兵馬都部署，武信軍節度、侍衛步軍都指揮使崔彥進充副都部署，樞密副使王仁贍充都監，龍捷右廂都指揮使史延德充馬軍都指揮使，虎捷右廂都指揮使張萬友充步軍都指揮使，隴州防禦使張凝充先鋒都指揮使，左神武大將軍王繼濤充濠砦使，內染院使康延澤充馬軍都監，翰林副使張煦充步軍都監，供奉官田仁朗充濠砦都監，殿直鄭粲充先鋒都監，步軍都軍頭向韜充先鋒都軍頭，寧江軍節度、侍衛馬步軍都指揮使劉廷讓充歸州路行營前軍兵馬副都部署，內客省使、樞密承旨曹彬充都監，客省使武懷節充戰棹部署，龍捷左廂都指揮使李進卿充步軍都指揮使，前階州刺史高彥暉充先鋒都指揮使，右衛將軍白廷誨充濠砦使，禦廚副使朱光緒充馬軍都監，儀鸞副使折彥贇充步軍都監，八作副使王令岩充先鋒都監，供奉官郝守濬充濠砦都監，馬步軍都軍頭楊光美充戰棹左右廂都指揮使，供奉官藥守節充戰棹左廂都監，殿直劉漢卿充戰棹右廂都監，率禁兵三萬人、諸州兵二萬人分路討之。

translations.literal: He then appointed Zhongwu Army military commissioner Wang Quanbin overall commander of the Fengzhou route forward army; Wuxin Army military commissioner and palace infantry commander Cui Yanjin as deputy commander; deputy privy councilor Wang Renzan as army inspector; Dragon Swift Right Wing commander Shi Yande as cavalry commander; Tiger Swift Right Wing commander Zhang Wanyou as infantry commander; Longzhou defense commissioner Zhang Ning as vanguard commander; Left Divine Martial grand general Wang Jitao as siege commissioner; Inner Dyeing Bureau commissioner Kang Yanze as cavalry inspector; Hanlin deputy academician Zhang Xu as infantry inspector; palace attendant Tian Renlang as siege inspector; palace attendant Zheng Can as vanguard inspector; infantry chief Xiang Tao as vanguard chief; Ningjiang Army military commissioner and palace horse-and-foot commander Liu Tingrang as deputy commander of the Guizhou route forward army; Inner Reception Bureau commissioner and privy councilor Cao Bin as army inspector; Reception Bureau commissioner Wu Huaijie as fleet commander; Dragon Swift Left Wing commander Li Jinqing as infantry commander; former Jiezhou prefect Gao Yanhui as vanguard commander; Right Guard general Bai Tinghui as siege commissioner; Imperial Kitchen deputy commissioner Zhu Guangxu as cavalry inspector; Ceremonial Guard deputy commissioner Zhe Yanyun as infantry inspector; Eight Works deputy commissioner Wang Lingyan as vanguard inspector; palace attendant Hao Shoujun as siege inspector; horse-and-foot army chief Yang Guangmei as commander of both fleet wings; palace attendant Yao Shoujie as left fleet inspector; palace attendant Liu Hanqing as right fleet inspector—and led thirty thousand palace troops and twenty thousand troops from the circuits in separate columns to attack.
translations.idiomatic: He then appointed Wang Quanbin, military commissioner of the Zhongwu Army, overall commander of the Fengzhou route forward army; Cui Yanjin, military commissioner of the Wuxin Army and commander of the palace infantry, as his deputy; Wang Renzan, deputy privy councilor, as army inspector; Shi Yande, commander of the Dragon Swift Right Wing, as cavalry commander; Zhang Wanyou, commander of the Tiger Swift Right Wing, as infantry commander; Zhang Ning, defense commissioner of Longzhou, as vanguard commander; Wang Jitao, grand general of the Left Divine Martial Army, as siege commissioner; Kang Yanze of the Inner Dyeing Bureau as cavalry inspector; Zhang Xu, Hanlin deputy academician, as infantry inspector; and a full roster of subordinate commanders and inspectors for the Guizhou route under Liu Tingrang and Cao Bin, with Wu Huaijie commanding the fleet and Yang Guangmei commanding both fleet wings—then sent them against Shu in separate columns with thirty thousand palace troops and twenty thousand circuit troops.

sentences.zh: 詔令孫遇等指畫江山曲折之狀，及兵砦戍守之處道裏遠近，俾畫工圖之，以授全斌等。

translations.literal: He ordered Sun Yu and the others to trace the winding course of rivers and mountains and the distances to fortified posts and garrisons, had painters draw maps, and gave them to Quanbin and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Sun Yu and the others to trace the winding course of rivers and mountains and the distances to fortified posts and garrisons, had painters draw maps, and gave them to Quanbin and his commanders.

sentences.zh: 因謂曰：“西川可取否？”

translations.literal: Thereupon he asked them: "West River Circuit—can it be taken?"
translations.idiomatic: He then asked them: "Can West River Circuit be taken?"

sentences.zh: 全斌等對曰：“臣等仗天威，遵廟算，刻日可定。”

translations.literal: Quanbin and the others replied: "We subjects rely on Heaven's majesty and follow the temple calculations; it can be settled within days."
translations.idiomatic: Quanbin and the others replied: "Your subjects rely on Heaven's majesty and follow the court's plan; it can be settled within days."

sentences.zh: 龍捷右廂都校史延德前奏曰：“西川一方，倘在天上，人不能到，固無可奈何。

translations.literal: Dragon Swift Right Wing commander Shi Yande stepped forward and said: "If West River Circuit were in the sky, where men could not reach it, nothing could be done.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yande, commander of the Dragon Swift Right Wing, stepped forward and said: "If West River Circuit were in the sky, where men could not reach it, nothing could be done.

sentences.zh: 若在地上，以今之兵力，到即平矣。”

translations.literal: If it is on the ground, with the forces we have now, wherever we reach, at once it will be pacified."
translations.idiomatic: But if it is on earth, with the forces we have now, wherever we arrive we shall pacify it at once."

sentences.zh: 上壯其言，謂之曰：“汝等果敢如此，我何憂乎！”

translations.literal: The emperor was heartened by his words and said to them: "If you are this bold and resolute; what have I to fear!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was heartened by his words and said to them: "If you are this bold and resolute, what have I to fear!"

sentences.zh: 又謂全斌等曰：“凡克城砦，止籍其器甲芻糧，悉艱錢帛分給戰士。”

translations.literal: He also told Quanbin and the others: "Every city or fort taken, register only its weapons, armor, fodder, and grain, and distribute all the money and silks among the fighting men.
translations.idiomatic: He also told Quanbin and the others: "Whenever you take a city or fort, register only its weapons, armor, fodder, and grain, and distribute all the money and silks among the fighting men.

sentences.zh: 及兵至，昶遣王昭遠、趙崇韜、韓保正、李進等來拒戰。

translations.literal: When the army arrived, Chang sent Wang Zhaoyuan, Zhao Chongtao, Han Baozheng, Li Jin, and others to oppose them.
translations.idiomatic: When the armies arrived, Chang sent Wang Zhaoyuan, Zhao Chongtao, Han Baozheng, Li Jin, and others to oppose them.

sentences.zh: 昭遠等相繼就擒，昶大懼，出金帛募兵，令其子玄喆統之，李廷珪、張惠安為其副，以守劍門。

translations.literal: Zhaoyuan and the rest were captured in succession; Chang greatly feared, offered gold and silks to recruit troops, and put his son Xuanzhe in overall command with Li Tinggui and Zhang Huian as deputies to hold Jianmen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyuan and the others were captured one after another; Chang was greatly afraid, offered gold and silks to recruit troops, and put his son Xuanzhe in overall command with Li Tinggui and Zhang Huian as deputies to hold Jianmen.

sentences.zh: 玄喆素不習武，廷珪、惠安皆庸懦無識。

translations.literal: Xuanzhe from of old did not practice military affairs; Tinggui and Huian were both mediocre, timid, and without judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzhe had never practiced warfare; Tinggui and Huian were both mediocre, timid, and without judgment.

sentences.zh: 玄喆離成都，但攜姬妾、樂器及伶人數十輩，晨夜嬉戲，不恤軍政。

translations.literal: When Xuanzhe left Chengdu he took only concubines; musical instruments; and several dozen entertainers; sporting day and night without regard for military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzhe left Chengdu he took only concubines, musical instruments, and several dozen entertainers, sporting day and night without regard for military affairs.

sentences.zh: 至綿州，聞宋師已破劍門，遂遁歸東川，所過焚廬舍倉稟而去。

translations.literal: On reaching Mianzhou and heard that Song forces had already broken through Jianmen, he fled back to East River Circuit, burning houses and granaries along the way as he went.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Mianzhou and heard that Song forces had already broken through Jianmen, he fled back to East River Circuit, burning houses and granaries along the way as he went.

sentences.zh: 昶益惶駭，問計於左右。

translations.literal: Chang was still more alarmed and asked his attendants for counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Chang grew still more terrified and asked his attendants for counsel.

sentences.zh: 有老將石斌，對以宋師遠來，勢不能久，請聚兵固守以老之。

translations.literal: An old general, Shi Bin, replied that the Song armies had come from afar and could not remain long, and asked to gather troops, hold fast, and wear them down.
translations.idiomatic: An old general named Shi Bin replied that the Song armies had come from afar and could not remain long, and asked to gather troops, hold fast, and wear them down.

sentences.zh: 昶曰：“吾父子以豐衣美食養士四十年，及遇敵，不能為我東向發一矢。

translations.literal: Chang said, "For forty years my father and I have clothed and fed our troops in comfort; yet when the enemy comes they will not for me shoot one arrow eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Chang said: "For forty years my father and I have clothed and fed our troops in comfort; yet when the enemy comes they will not loose a single arrow eastward for me.

sentences.zh: 今若固壘，何人為我效命？”

translations.literal: Now if we fortify the camps, who will for me give their lives?
translations.idiomatic: If we now hold the forts, who will die for me?

sentences.zh: 三年正月，昶遣其通奏伊審征齎表詣全斌請降，且言：“中外骨肉二百餘人，有親年幾七十，願終甘旨之養，免賜睽離之責，則祖宗血食庶獲少延。”

translations.literal: First month, year third, Chang sent his memorial courier Yi Shenzheng with a petition to Quanbin to surrender, saying: "Within and without my clan are more than two hundred kin; some elders are nearly seventy, and I wish them to end their days in comfort and avoid the punishment of separation, so that our ancestral sacrifices may yet continue a little longer."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year, Chang sent his memorial courier Yi Shenzheng with a petition to Quanbin to surrender, saying: "Within and without my clan are more than two hundred kin; some elders are nearly seventy, and I wish them to end their days in comfort and avoid the punishment of separation, so that our ancestral sacrifices may yet continue a little longer."

sentences.zh: 末援劉禪、陳叔寶故事以請封號。

translations.literal: At the end he cited Liu Shan and Chen Shubao precedents to request enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: At the end he cited the precedents of Liu Shan and Chen Shubao to request an enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 全斌等既受其降，遣馬軍都監康延澤先以百騎入城見昶，諭以恩信，留三日，盡封府庫而還。

translations.literal: Quanbin and the others, having accepted his surrender, they sent cavalry inspector Kang Yanze ahead with a hundred horsemen into the city to see Chang, reassure him of imperial favor, and after three days seal all treasuries and withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: After Quanbin and the others accepted his surrender, they sent cavalry inspector Kang Yanze ahead with a hundred horsemen into the city to see Chang, reassure him of imperial favor, and after three days seal all treasuries and withdraw.

sentences.zh: 昶又遣其弟仁贄詣闕上表言：

translations.literal: Chang again sent his younger brother Renzhi to the court with a memorial stating:
translations.idiomatic: Chang also sent his younger brother Renzhi to the court with a memorial stating:

sentences.zh: 先臣受命唐室，建牙蜀川，因時事之變更，為人心之擁迫。

translations.literal: My late father received his commission from the Tang house and raised his standard in Shu; compelled by the changes of the times and the pressure of popular sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: My late father received his commission from the Tang house and raised his standard in Shu, compelled by the changes of the times and the pressure of popular sentiment.

sentences.zh: 先臣即世，臣方丱年，猥以童昏，繆承餘緒。

translations.literal: When the late father died, I was still in childhood topknots; foolishly I inherited what he left.
translations.idiomatic: When my late father passed away I was still a child in topknots; in my youthful folly I wrongly inherited what he left.

sentences.zh: 乖以小事大之禮，闕稱藩奉國之誠，染習偷安，因循積歲。

translations.literal: I violated the rite of small serving great and lacked the sincerity of a vassal honoring the realm, growing accustomed to ease and dragging on year after year.
translations.idiomatic: I failed the propriety of a small state serving a great one and lacked the sincerity of a vassal honoring the realm, growing accustomed to ease and dragging on year after year.

sentences.zh: 所以上煩宸算，遠發王師，勢甚疾雷，功如破竹。

translations.literal: Therefore I troubled the imperial mind and drew royal armies from afar; their momentum was like swift thunder; their achievement like bamboo split.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I troubled the imperial mind and drew royal armies from afar; their momentum was like sudden thunder, their achievement like splitting bamboo.

sentences.zh: 顧惟懦卒，焉敢當鋒？

translations.literal: Looking at my weak soldiers, how dare I face the blades?
translations.idiomatic: Considering only my feeble troops, how could I dare meet the spearpoints?

sentences.zh: 尋束手以雲歸，止傾心而俟命。

translations.literal: Soon I bound my hands and came, like clouds returning; I could only incline my heart and await your command.
translations.idiomatic: Soon I bound my hands and came like clouds returning; I could only incline my heart and await your command.

sentences.zh: 今月七日，已令私署通奏使、宣徽南院使伊審征奉表歸降，以緣路寇攘，前進不得。

translations.literal: This month, day seventh, I had my private memorial courier, Southern Court commissioner of the Xuanhui Bureau Yi Shenzheng, present a petition of surrender; because bandits troubled the route he could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh of this month I had my private memorial courier, Southern Court commissioner of the Xuanhui Bureau Yi Shenzheng, present a petition of surrender; because bandits troubled the route he could not advance.

sentences.zh: 臣尋更令兵士援送，至十一日，尚恐前表未達，續遣供奉官王茂隆再齎前表。

translations.literal: I then ordered soldiers to escort him forward; by the eleventh; still fearing the earlier petition had not arrived; I sent palace attendant Wang Maolong again with the former petition.
translations.idiomatic: I then ordered soldiers to escort him forward; by the eleventh, still fearing the earlier petition had not arrived, I sent palace attendant Wang Maolong again with the former petition.

sentences.zh: 至十二日以後，相次方到軍前，必料血誠，上達睿聽。

translations.literal: From the twelfth day onward they reached the army in succession; I trust blood-sincerity has ascended to the sage ear.
translations.idiomatic: From the twelfth onward they reached the army one after another; I trust my loyal sincerity has reached your sage hearing.

sentences.zh: 臣今月十九日，已領親男諸弟，納降禮於軍門，至於老母諸孫，延餘喘於私第。

translations.literal: On the nineteenth of this month I have already led my sons and younger brothers to perform the rites of surrender at the army gate; as for my aged mother and grandsons; they linger on in our private residence.
translations.idiomatic: On the nineteenth of this month I have already led my sons and younger brothers to perform the rites of surrender at the army gate; as for my aged mother and grandsons, they linger on in our private residence.

sentences.zh: 陛下至仁廣覆，大德好生，顧臣假息於數年，所望全軀於此日。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's utmost benevolence spreads wide; your great virtue cherishes life; you have granted me a few years' reprieve; and what I hope for on this day is to keep my person whole.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's utmost benevolence spreads wide, your great virtue cherishes life; you have granted me a few years' reprieve, and what I hope for on this day is to keep my person whole.

sentences.zh: 今蒙元戎慰恤，監護撫安，若非天地之垂慈，豈見軍民之受賜！

translations.literal: Now I have received the commander-in-chief's consolation and care; his protection and reassurance; had Heaven and Earth not shown mercy; how could soldiers and people have received such bounty!
translations.idiomatic: Now I have received the commander-in-chief's consolation and care, his protection and reassurance; had Heaven and Earth not shown mercy, how could soldiers and people have received such bounty!

sentences.zh: 臣亦自量過咎，尚切憂疑，謹遣親弟詣闕奉表，待罪以聞。

translations.literal: I too measured my own faults and still felt keen worry; I respectfully sent my younger brother to court with a memorial, reporting guilt to be heard.
translations.idiomatic: I too measure my own faults and still feel keen anxiety; I respectfully send my younger brother to court with this memorial to report my guilt and await judgment.

sentences.zh: 太祖詔曰：

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor's edict said:
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor's edict read:

sentences.zh: 朕以受命上穹，臨製中土，姑務保民而崇德，豈思右武以佳兵？

translations.literal: We; having received Heaven's mandate; govern the central realm; we first seek to protect the people and exalt virtue—how would we delight in force and prize arms?
translations.idiomatic: We, having received Heaven's mandate, govern the central realm; we first seek to protect the people and exalt virtue—how would we delight in force and prize arms?

sentences.zh: 至於臨戎，蓋非獲已。

translations.literal: As for taking the field; it is surely not what we would choose.
translations.idiomatic: As for taking the field, it is surely not what we would choose.

sentences.zh: 矧惟益部，僻處一隅，靡思僭竊之愆，輒肆窺覦之誌，潛結並寇，自啟釁端。

translations.literal: Especially as Yi Region sits remote in a corner; never reflecting on the crime of usurpation but rashly indulging designs of encroachment; secretly allying with the Bingzhou bandit and opening the breach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Especially as Yi Region sits remote in a corner, never reflecting on the crime of usurpation but rashly indulging designs of encroachment, secretly allying with the Bingzhou bandit and opening the breach themselves.

sentences.zh: 爰命偏師，往申吊伐，靈旗所指，逆壘自平。

translations.literal: We therefore ordered a detached force to carry out punitive consolation; wherever the sacred banners pointed; rebel strongholds fell of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore ordered a detached force to carry out punitive consolation; wherever the sacred banners pointed, rebel strongholds fell of themselves.

sentences.zh: 朕嚐中宵憮然，兆民何罪！

translations.literal: We have lain wakeful at midnight in distress—what crime have the myriad people committed!
translations.idiomatic: We have lain wakeful at midnight in distress—what crime had the myriad people committed!

sentences.zh: 屢馳馹騎，嚴戒兵鋒，務宣拯溺之懷，以盡招攜之禮。

translations.literal: Again and again we sent post riders and strictly restrained the army's edge; striving to proclaim the will to rescue the drowning and fully perform the rites of winning men over.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again we sent post riders and strictly restrained the army's edge, striving to proclaim the will to rescue the drowning and fully perform the rites of winning men over.

sentences.zh: 而卿果能率官屬而請命，拜表疏以祈恩，托以慈親，保其宗祀，悉封庫府，以待王師。

translations.literal: And you were indeed able to lead your officials in begging for mercy; present petitions to seek grace; entrust your aged mother; preserve your ancestral sacrifices; and seal all treasuries to await the royal army.
translations.idiomatic: And you were indeed able to lead your officials in begging for mercy, present petitions to seek grace, entrust your aged mother, preserve your ancestral sacrifices, and seal all treasuries to await the royal army.

sentences.zh: 追咎改圖，將自求於多福；

translations.literal: Repenting of past faults and changing course; you will seek greater blessings for yourself;
translations.idiomatic: Repenting of past faults and changing course, you will seek greater blessings for yourself;

sentences.zh: 匿瑕含垢，當盡滌於前非。

translations.literal: concealing flaws and bearing stains; your former wrongs shall be fully washed away.
translations.idiomatic: concealing flaws and bearing stains, your former wrongs shall be fully washed away.

sentences.zh: 朕不食言，爾無他慮。

translations.literal: We do not break our word—you must have no other anxieties.
translations.idiomatic: We do not eat our words—have no other anxieties.

sentences.zh: 昶乃舉族與官屬由峽江而下，至江陵，上遣皇城使竇思儼迎勞之。

translations.literal: Chang then led clan and officials by the Gorge River downward; at Jiangling the emperor sent Palace Commissioner Dou Siyan to welcome and comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: Chang then led his entire clan and officials down the Gorges River; at Jiangling the emperor sent palace commissioner Dou Siyan to welcome and comfort them.

sentences.zh: 四月初，昶與母至襄漢，復遣使齎詔賜茶藥。

translations.literal: Early in the fourth month Chang and his mother reached Xiang and Han; the emperor again sent envoys bearing an edict granting tea and medicine.
translations.idiomatic: In early fourth month Chang and his mother reached Xiang and Han; the emperor again sent envoys with an edict granting tea and medicine.

sentences.zh: 所賜詔不名，仍呼昶母為國母。

translations.literal: The edict of gift did not name him; and still addressed Chang's mother as the state mother.
translations.idiomatic: The edict of gift did not name him, and still addressed Chang's mother as the state mother.

sentences.zh: 昶將至，命太宗勞於近郊。

translations.literal: As Chang was about to arrive, he ordered the Taizong to welcome him in the near suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: As Chang was about to arrive, he ordered Taizong to welcome him in the near suburbs.

sentences.zh: 昶率子弟素服待罪闕下，太祖禦崇元殿，備禮見之，賜昶襲衣、玉帶、黃金鞍勒馬、金器千兩、銀器萬兩、錦綺千段、絹萬匹；

translations.literal: Chang led his sons and younger brothers in plain dress to await judgment below the palace; the Founding Emperor received him in full ceremony at the Chongyuan Hall and granted Chang court robes; jade belt; horse with golden saddle and bridle; a thousand taels of gold vessels; ten thousand taels of silver vessels, a thousand lengths of brocade silk, and ten thousand bolts of silk;
translations.idiomatic: Chang led his sons and younger brothers in plain dress to await judgment below the palace; the Founding Emperor received him in full ceremony at the Chongyuan Hall and granted Chang court robes, jade belt, horse with golden saddle and bridle, a thousand taels of gold vessels, ten thousand taels of silver vessels, a thousand lengths of brocade silk, and ten thousand bolts of silk;

sentences.zh: 又賜昶母金器三百兩、銀器三千兩、錦綺千匹、絹千匹；

translations.literal: he also granted Chang's mother three hundred taels of gold vessels; three thousand taels of silver vessels, a thousand lengths of brocade silk, and a thousand bolts of silk;
translations.idiomatic: he also granted Chang's mother three hundred taels of gold vessels, three thousand taels of silver vessels, a thousand lengths of brocade silk, and a thousand bolts of silk;

sentences.zh: 子弟及其官屬等襲衣、金玉帶、鞍勒馬、車乘、器幣有差；

translations.literal: sons; younger brothers, and officials received court robes, jade belts, saddled horses, carriages, and vessels in varying measure;
translations.idiomatic: sons, younger brothers, and officials received court robes, jade belts, saddled horses, carriages, and vessels in varying measure;

sentences.zh: 又遣使分詣江陵、鳳翔賜其家屬錢帛，疾病者給以醫藥。

translations.literal: envoys were also sent separately to Jiangling and Fengxiang to grant money and silks to their families; and the sick were given medicine.
translations.idiomatic: envoys were also sent separately to Jiangling and Fengxiang to grant money and silks to their families, and the sick were given medicine.

sentences.zh: 即日宴於大明殿。

translations.literal: That same day: a banquet in the Daming Hall.
translations.idiomatic: That same day a banquet was held in the Daming Hall.

sentences.zh: 先是，詔有司於右掖門外，臨汴水起大第五百間以待昶，供帳悉備，至是賜之，又為其官屬各營居第。

translations.literal: Earlier an edict had ordered the authorities to build five hundred great rooms outside the Right Flank Gate facing the Bian River to await Chang; with all furnishings complete; these were now granted to him; and residences were also built for each of his officials.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier an edict had ordered the authorities to build five hundred great rooms outside the Right Flank Gate facing the Bian River to await Chang, with all furnishings complete; these were now granted to him, and residences were also built for each of his officials.

sentences.zh: 翌日，詔曰：

translations.literal: The next day an edict said:
translations.idiomatic: The next day an edict proclaimed:

sentences.zh: 伯禹導川，黑水本梁州之域；

translations.literal: Yu the Great channeled the rivers; the Black River was originally within Liang Province;
translations.idiomatic: When Yu the Great channeled the rivers, the Black River lay within Liang Province;

sentences.zh: 《河圖》括象，岷山直井絡之墟。

translations.literal: the River Chart embraces its symbols; and Mount Min stands at the heart of the Well-Cord region.
translations.idiomatic: the River Chart embraces its symbols, and Mount Min stands at the heart of the Well-Cord region.

sentences.zh: 是曰坤維，素為王土。

translations.literal: This is called the southwestern quarter and has long been royal soil.
translations.idiomatic: This southwestern quarter has long been imperial domain.

sentences.zh: 屬中原多故，四海群飛，遂剖裂於山河，競僭竊於位號。

translations.literal: When the central plain suffered many troubles and all within the four seas rose in flight, it was carved apart by mountains and rivers and men vied in usurping titles.
translations.idiomatic: When turmoil engulfed the central plain and the realm broke into flight, the land was carved apart by mountains and rivers as men vied to usurp imperial titles.

sentences.zh: 朕削平宇縣，載整皇綱，復周、漢之舊疆，寵綏群後；

translations.literal: We have cut down and pacified the realm, restored the imperial order, recovered the old frontiers of Zhou and Han, and graciously reassured the feudal lords;
translations.idiomatic: We have pacified the realm, restored the imperial order, recovered the old frontiers of Zhou and Han, and graciously reassured the feudal lords;

sentences.zh: 采唐、虞之大訓，協和萬邦。

translations.literal: we have adopted Tang and Yu's great instructions and brought the myriad states into harmony.
translations.idiomatic: we have taken the great lessons of Tang and Yu and brought the myriad states into harmony.

sentences.zh: 六年於茲，百揆時敘。

translations.literal: Six years have passed here, and the hundred offices proceed in their seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Six years have now passed, and the hundred offices proceed in good order.

sentences.zh: 禮樂征伐之柄，盡出朝廷；

translations.literal: the authority over rites, music, punitive expeditions, and campaigns issues entirely from the court;
translations.idiomatic: The authority over rites, music, and war rested entirely with the court;

sentences.zh: 蠻夷山海之君，鹹修職貢。

translations.literal: the lords of barbarians beyond the mountains and seas all maintain their tribute duties.
translations.idiomatic: the lords of distant lands beyond the mountains and seas all maintain their tribute duties.

sentences.zh: 一昨順長庚而授律，法時雨以興師，先申誕告之文，以慰徯來之眾。

translations.literal: Just yesterday, following the Metal Star, we set the pitch-pipes; modeling the timely rain, we raised armies; we first proclaimed the text of birth-announcement to comfort the people who had long awaited us.
translations.idiomatic: Only yesterday, following the Metal Star, we set the pitch-pipes and, like timely rain, raised armies; we first proclaimed our mandate to comfort the people who had long awaited us.

sentences.zh: 谘爾偽蜀主孟昶，克承餘緒，保據一隅，擅正朔以自尊，曆歲時而滋久。

translations.literal: We address you, false lord of Shu Meng Chang, who inherited what remained and held a corner of the realm, arrogating the calendar to exalt yourself through many years.
translations.idiomatic: We address you, the false lord of Shu, Meng Chang, who inherited what remained and held a corner of the realm, arrogating the calendar to exalt yourself through many years.

sentences.zh: 屬王師致討，察天道之惡盈，體此綏懷，思於效順，盡率群吏，降於軍門。

translations.literal: When the royal army came to punish you, perceiving that Heaven's way abhors excess, you grasped this reassurance, resolved to submit, led all your officials, and surrendered at the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the royal army came to punish you, seeing that Heaven abhors excess, you grasped our reassurance, resolved to submit, led all your officials, and surrendered at the army gate.

sentences.zh: 抗手疏以陳誠，伏天閽而請命。

translations.literal: You raised a hand memorial to declare sincerity and bowed at Heaven's Gate to beg for orders.
translations.idiomatic: You raised a written memorial to declare your sincerity and bowed at Heaven's gate to beg for mercy.

sentences.zh: 是用昭示大信，盡滌疵瑕，度越彝章，升於崇秩。

translations.literal: Therefore We proclaim great trust; wash away all flaws; transcend the regular statutes; and raise you to exalted rank.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore We proclaim great trust, wash away all flaws, transcend the regular statutes, and raise you to exalted rank.

sentences.zh: 冠紫微之近署，以奉內朝；

translations.literal: You shall head offices near the Purple Palace to serve the inner court;
translations.idiomatic: You shall stand at the head of offices near the Purple Palace to serve the inner court;

sentences.zh: 剪鶉首之奧區，為之封邑。

translations.literal: We cut from the Quail's Head deep region a fief for your enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: We cut from the deep region of the Quail's Head a fief for your enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 率從異數，式洽殊私。

translations.literal: Follow these extraordinary measures and receive this special favor.
translations.idiomatic: Accept these extraordinary honors and receive this special favor.

sentences.zh: 爾宜欽承，往踐厥位。

translations.literal: You ought respectfully receive this and go tread your post.
translations.idiomatic: You should respectfully receive this and go to take up your post.

sentences.zh: 可開府儀同三司、檢校太師兼中書令、秦國公，給上鎮節度使奉祿。

translations.literal: You are appointed Grand Preceptor of the First Rank with the privilege of an independent office; honorary Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat, Duke of Qin, with the stipend of a first-rank military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: You are appointed Grand Preceptor of the First Rank with the privilege of an independent office, honorary Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat, Duke of Qin, with the stipend of a first-rank military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 餘官除拜有差。

translations.literal: The remaining offices are conferred with differences.
translations.idiomatic: Other offices are conferred in varying measure.

sentences.zh: 昶數日卒，年四十七。

translations.literal: Chang died within several days, aged forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Chang died within several days, at the age of forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 太祖廢朝五日，素服發哀於大明殿。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor ceased court for five days; in plain dress he raised mourning in the Daming Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor suspended court for five days and in plain dress proclaimed mourning in the Daming Hall.

sentences.zh: 賜尚書令，追封楚王，諡恭孝，賻布帛千匹，葬事官給。

translations.literal: He was granted the title Director of the Secretariat, posthumously enfeoffed as King of Chu, given the posthumous name Gongxiao, and granted a thousand bolts of silks for funeral gifts; burial expenses were supplied by the state.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the title Director of the Secretariat, posthumously enfeoffed as King of Chu with the posthumous name Gongxiao, and granted a thousand bolts of silks for funeral gifts; burial expenses were supplied by the state.

sentences.zh: 後數日，其母李氏亦卒。

translations.literal: Several days later his mother, the Lady Li, also died.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later his mother, Lady Li, also died.

sentences.zh: 初，李氏隨昶至京師，太祖數命肩輿入宮，謂之曰：“母善自愛，無戚戚懷鄉土，異日當送母歸。”

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Lady Li followed Chang to the capital, the Founding Emperor repeatedly ordered a palanquin to bring her into the palace and told her: "Mother, take good care of yourself; do not grieve over your homeland—I shall send you home another day."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Lady Li followed Chang to the capital, the Founding Emperor repeatedly had her carried into the palace in a palanquin and told her: "Mother, take good care of yourself; do not grieve over your homeland—I shall send you home another day."

sentences.zh: 李氏曰：“使妾安往？”

translations.literal: The Lady Li said: "Whither should your servant go?"
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li said: "Where should I go?"

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：“歸蜀爾。”

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor said: "Return to Shu."
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor said: "Back to Shu."

sentences.zh: 李氏曰：“妾家本太原，倘得歸老並土，妾之願也。”

translations.literal: The Lady Li said: "Your servant's family is originally from Taiyuan; if I could end my days on Bing soil, that would be my wish."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li said: "My family is originally from Taiyuan; if I could end my days in Bing territory, that would be my wish."

sentences.zh: 時晉陽未平，太祖聞其言大喜，曰：“俟平劉鈞，即如母所願。”

translations.literal: At that time Jinyang had not yet been pacified; hearing her words the Founding Emperor was greatly pleased and said: "When Liu Jun is pacified, I shall do as Mother wishes."
translations.idiomatic: Jinyang had not yet been pacified; hearing her words the Founding Emperor was greatly pleased and said: "When Liu Jun is pacified, I shall do as you wish."

sentences.zh: 因厚加賜賚。

translations.literal: Thereupon he added rich gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore granted her rich gifts.

sentences.zh: 及昶卒，不哭，以酒酹地曰：“汝不能死社稷，貪生以至今日。

translations.literal: When Chang died she did not weep; she poured wine on the ground and said: "You could not die for the altars of state but clung to life until today.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang died she did not weep but poured wine on the ground and said: "You could not die for the altars of state but clung to life until today.

sentences.zh: 吾所以忍死者，以汝在爾。

translations.literal: The reason I endured death was because you were still alive.
translations.idiomatic: The reason I endured living was because you were still alive.

sentences.zh: 今汝既死，吾何生焉！”

translations.literal: Now that you are dead, why should I live!"
translations.idiomatic: Now that you are dead, why should I go on living!"

sentences.zh: 因不食，數日卒。

translations.literal: Thereupon she refused food; within several days she died.
translations.idiomatic: She therefore refused food and died within several days.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞而傷之，賻贈加等。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor; hearing of it, was grieved and increased the funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor, hearing of it, was grieved and increased the funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 令鴻臚卿範禹偁護喪事，與昶俱葬洛陽，詔發奉義甲士千人護送。

translations.literal: He ordered Court of State Ceremonial director Fan Yucheng to oversee the funeral; she was buried with Chang at Luoyang; an edict sent a thousand soldiers of the Fengyi Guard to escort them.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Court of State Ceremonial director Fan Yucheng to oversee the funeral and buried her with Chang at Luoyang; an edict sent a thousand soldiers of the Fengyi Guard to escort them.

sentences.zh: 七月，正衙備禮冊命昶，其文曰：

translations.literal: In the seventh month; at the main court with full ceremony; Chang was enfeoffed by patent; the text read:
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, at the main court with full ceremony, Chang was enfeoffed by patent; the text read:

sentences.zh: 維乾德三年，歲次乙丑，七月己巳朔，二十四日戊子，皇帝若曰：“谘故檢校太師兼中書令、秦國公孟昶，冊贈之典，所以彰世祚而紀勳伐，繼絕之義，所以旌異域而表來庭。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qiande, the year yichou, on the first day jisi of the seventh month, the twenty-fourth day wuzi, the emperor spoke thus: "We address the late honorary Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat, Duke of Qin Meng Chang: the rite of enfeoffment by patent displays a dynasty's standing and records merit; the principle of continuing a broken line honors distant realms and marks those who come to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Qiande, on the twenty-fourth day of the seventh month, the emperor spoke thus: "We address the late honorary Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat, Duke of Qin, Meng Chang: the rite of enfeoffment by patent displays a dynasty's standing and records merit; the principle of continuing a broken line honors distant realms and marks those who come to court.

sentences.zh: 苟匪全功，寧兼二者。

translations.literal: If the merit is not complete, how can both be joined?
translations.idiomatic: If the merit is not complete, how can both honors be joined?

sentences.zh: 國家乘乾撫運，括地開圖。

translations.literal: Our state rides the Qian hexagram to govern the age, embraces the land, and opens the map.
translations.idiomatic: Our state rides Heaven's mandate to govern the age, embraces the land, and opens the map.

sentences.zh: 稽至德於勳、華，體深仁於湯、禹。

translations.literal: We examine the utmost virtue of Kun and Hua and embody the deep benevolence of Tang and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: We examine the utmost virtue of Emperor Shun and Emperor Yao and embody the deep benevolence of Tang and Yu.

sentences.zh: 既定壺關之亂，復剪淮夷之凶，暨荊及衡，洗蕩逋穢。

translations.literal: Having settled the turmoil of Huguan, we again cut down the evil of the Huai barbarians; reaching Jing and Heng, we washed away the fleeing filth.
translations.idiomatic: Having settled the turmoil of Huguan, we again cut down the Huai rebels; reaching Jing and Heng, we washed away the fleeing filth.

sentences.zh: 以為君人之道，先德而後刑；

translations.literal: We hold that the way of ruling men puts virtue first and punishment after;
translations.idiomatic: We hold that the way of ruling puts virtue first and punishment after;

sentences.zh: 王者之師，有征而無戰。

translations.literal: the army of a true king campaigns but does not fight.
translations.idiomatic: the army of a true king campaigns but does not need to fight.

sentences.zh: 兵威震疊，寰宇來同。

translations.literal: Military might shook the layered realms; the whole realm came to unity.
translations.idiomatic: Military might shook the layered realms and the whole universe came to unity.

sentences.zh: 以至薄伐兩川，徂征三峽。

translations.literal: Thus we lightly chastised the two river circuits and marched against the Three Gorges.
translations.idiomatic: Thus we lightly punished the two river circuits and marched against the Three Gorges.

sentences.zh: 惟爾昶襲乃堂構，據有巴庸，而能祗畏皇靈，保全宗緒，知機識變，委順圖全。

translations.literal: You alone, Chang, inherited your father's hall and beams and held Ba and Yong, yet were able to revere the imperial numen, preserve your ancestral line, know the moment and read change, submit in compliance and seek wholeness.
translations.idiomatic: You alone, Chang, inherited your father's house and held Ba and Yong, yet were able to revere the imperial numen, preserve your ancestral line, know the moment and read change, submit in compliance and seek wholeness.

sentences.zh: 馳子牟魏闕之心，奉伯禹塗山之會。

translations.literal: You sped the heart of Zimu toward the Wei gate and offered the assembly of Yu the Great at Mount Tu.
translations.idiomatic: You sped the heart of Zimu toward the imperial gate and offered the assembly of Yu the Great at Mount Tu.

sentences.zh: 朕自聞獻款，良切虛懷。

translations.literal: From the moment We heard your offering of sincerity; Our open heart was deeply moved.
translations.idiomatic: From the moment We heard your offering of sincerity, Our open heart was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 舟車欣至止之初，邸第錫非常之製。

translations.literal: When carriage and boat joyfully arrived at their stopping place, We granted an extraordinary lodge.
translations.idiomatic: When you joyfully arrived by carriage and boat, We granted an extraordinary lodge.

sentences.zh: 封崇異數，祈保永年。

translations.literal: We enfeoffed you with extraordinary honors and prayed for long years.
translations.idiomatic: We enfeoffed you with extraordinary honors and prayed you might keep long years.

sentences.zh: 景命不融，奄然殂謝。

translations.literal: The bright mandate did not blend; suddenly you passed away.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's bright mandate did not hold; suddenly you passed away.

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 爾有及親之孝，特異常倫；

translations.literal: You had filial piety that reached your kin; surpassing ordinary measure;
translations.idiomatic: You had filial piety that reached your kin, surpassing ordinary measure;

sentences.zh: 爾有達上之情，所期終養。

translations.literal: you had feeling that reached your sovereign; hoping to support her to the end.
translations.idiomatic: you had feeling that reached your sovereign, hoping to support her to the end.

sentences.zh: 何高穹之不祐，與幽壤之同歸！

translations.literal: Why did the high vault not protect you, that you return to the dark earth together!
translations.idiomatic: Why did Heaven not protect you, that you return to the dark earth together!

sentences.zh: 斯朕所以當寧興悲，徹縣永歎。

translations.literal: This is why We; sitting in repose, rise in grief and suspend the music of the districts in lasting lament.
translations.idiomatic: This is why We, sitting in repose, rise in grief and suspend the music of the districts in lasting lament.

sentences.zh: 詢於史氏，申命禮官，今遣使起復雲麾將軍、檢校太傅、右神武統軍、兼御史大夫、上柱國、平昌縣開國伯食邑七百戶孟仁贄持節，冊贈爾為尚書令，仍追封楚王。

translations.literal: We consulted the historiographers and charged the ritual officers; We now send the envoy, restored from mourning, Cloud Banner General, honorary Grand Mentor, commander of the Right Divine Martial Army, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, Supreme Pillar of State, Baron of Pingchang with a fief of seven hundred households Meng Renzhi bearing credentials to enfeoff you posthumously as Director of the Secretariat and further enfeoff you as King of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: We consulted the historiographers and charged the ritual officers; We now send Meng Renzhi, restored from mourning—Cloud Banner General, honorary Grand Mentor, commander of the Right Divine Martial Army, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, Supreme Pillar of State, and Baron of Pingchang with a fief of seven hundred households—bearing credentials to enfeoff you posthumously as Director of the Secretariat and further as King of Chu.

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 式備哀榮，載光簡牒。

translations.literal: Thus complete the mourning honors and let them shine upon the bamboo and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Thus complete the mourning honors and let them shine upon the records.

sentences.zh: 南宮峻秩，全楚大邦，並示追崇，敻超彝製。

translations.literal: The lofty rank of the Southern Palace and the great state of all Chu together show posthumous elevation; far surpassing the regular statutes.
translations.idiomatic: The lofty rank of the Southern Palace and the great state of all Chu together show posthumous elevation, far surpassing the regular statutes.

sentences.zh: 始終之分，朕無愧焉。

translations.literal: In the bond from beginning to end; We have no shame.
translations.idiomatic: In the bond from beginning to end, We have no shame.

sentences.zh: 仍贈昶墳莊一區，給守墳人米千石，錢五萬。

translations.literal: We further granted Chang one estate for his tomb; a thousand piculs of grain for tomb keepers; and fifty thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: We further granted Chang one estate for his tomb, a thousand piculs of grain for tomb keepers, and fifty thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 初，昶在蜀專務奢靡，為七寶溺器，他物稱是。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Chang was in Shu he devoted himself to luxury, making chamber pots of the seven treasures, and other objects to match.
translations.idiomatic: While Chang ruled in Shu he devoted himself to luxury, making chamber pots of the seven treasures, and other objects to match.

sentences.zh: 每歲除，命學士為詞，題桃符，置寢門左右。

translations.literal: Every New Year's Eve he ordered academicians to compose verses, inscribe them on peach talismans, and place them to left and right of the bedchamber door.
translations.idiomatic: Every New Year's Eve he ordered academicians to compose verses, inscribe them on peach talismans, and place them on either side of the bedchamber door.

sentences.zh: 末年，學士幸寅遜撰詞，昶以其非工，自命筆題云：“新年納餘慶，喜節號長春。”

translations.literal: In his last year the academician Xing Yinxun composed the verse; Chang; finding it unskilled; took up the brush himself and wrote: "The new year receives remaining blessings; the festive season is called Everlasting Spring."
translations.idiomatic: In his last year the academician Xing Yinxun composed the verse; Chang, finding it unskilled, took up the brush himself and wrote: "The new year receives remaining blessings; the festive season is called Everlasting Spring."

sentences.zh: 以其年正月十一日降，太祖命呂餘慶知成都府，而“長春”乃聖節名也。

translations.literal: In that year; on the eleventh day of the first month; he surrendered; the Founding Emperor appointed Lü Yuqing prefect of Chengdu—and "Everlasting Spring" was the name of the sacred festival.
translations.idiomatic: In that year, on the eleventh day of the first month, he surrendered; the Founding Emperor appointed Lü Yuqing prefect of Chengdu—and "Everlasting Spring" was the name of the sacred festival.

sentences.zh: 又昶襲位後，民質錢取息者，將徙居，必署其門曰：“召主收贖。”

translations.literal: After Chang succeeded; when people who had pawned money for interest were about to move away; they had to post on their doors: "Summon the owner to redeem."
translations.idiomatic: After Chang succeeded, when people who had pawned money for interest were about to move away, they had to post on their doors: "Summon the owner to redeem."

sentences.zh: 周世宗平淮甸，克關南，即議討蜀而未果，至太祖乃平之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong of Zhou pacified the Huai region and took Guannan; and at once deliberated attacking Shu but did not succeed; only under the Founding Emperor was it pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong of Zhou pacified the Huai region and took Guannan, and at once deliberated attacking Shu but did not succeed; only under the Founding Emperor was it pacified.

sentences.zh: 昶三子：玄喆、玄玨、玄寶。

translations.literal: Chang's three sons: Xuanzhe, Xuanjue, and Xuanbao.
translations.idiomatic: Chang had three sons: Xuanzhe, Xuanjue, and Xuanbao.

sentences.zh: 玄寶先卒，僭贈遂王。

translations.literal: Xuanbao died first; posthumously enfeoffed as King of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanbao died first and was posthumously enfeoffed as King of Sui.

sentences.zh: 昶弟：仁贄、仁裕、仁操。

translations.literal: Chang's younger brothers: Renzhi, Renyu, and Rencao.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's younger brothers were Renzhi, Renyu, and Rencao.

sentences.zh: 昶既降，寧江軍節度、同平章事伊審征，檢校太尉兼侍中韓保正，山南西道節度、同平章事王昭遠，工部侍郎幸寅遜，武信軍節度、保寧軍都巡檢使李廷珪來闕下。

translations.literal: After Chang surrendered, Ningjiang Army military commissioner and co-equal councilor Yi Shenzheng, honorary Grand Marshal and Palace Attendant Han Baozheng, Shannan West Circuit military commissioner and co-equal councilor Wang Zhaoyuan, Vice Minister of Works Xing Yinxun, and Wuxin Army military commissioner and Baoning Army chief inspector Li Tinggui came to court.
translations.idiomatic: After Chang surrendered, Yi Shenzheng, Ningjiang Army military commissioner and co-equal councilor; Han Baozheng, honorary Grand Marshal and Palace Attendant; Wang Zhaoyuan, Shannan West Circuit military commissioner and co-equal councilor; Xing Yinxun, Vice Minister of Works; and Li Tinggui, Wuxin Army military commissioner and Baoning Army chief inspector, came to court.

sentences.zh: 審征授靜難軍節度，昭遠授左領軍衛大將軍，寅遜授右庶子，廷珪授右千牛衛上將軍，韓保正未授官卒。

translations.literal: Shenzheng was made military commissioner of the Jingnan Army; Zhaoyuan was made grand general of the Left Leading Army Guard; Yinxun was made right deputy heir apparent; Tinggui was made senior general of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard; Han Baozheng died before an office was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzheng was appointed military commissioner of the Jingnan Army; Zhaoyuan was appointed grand general of the Left Leading Army Guard; Yinxun was appointed right deputy heir apparent; Tinggui was appointed senior general of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard; Han Baozheng died before receiving an appointment.

sentences.zh: 保正、昭遠、廷珪，川中各有田宅，詔各賜錢三百萬。

translations.literal: Baozheng; Zhaoyuan; and Tinggui each had fields and houses in the river circuits; an edict granted each three million cash.
translations.idiomatic: Baozheng, Zhaoyuan, and Tinggui each had fields and houses in the river circuits; an edict granted each three million cash.

sentences.zh: 又成都人王處瓊，少孤，有司籍其金寶，昶降，輦送闕下。

translations.literal: Also Wang Chuqiong of Chengdu; orphaned in youth; had his gold and jewels registered by the authorities; when Chang surrendered they were carted to court.
translations.idiomatic: Also Wang Chuqiong of Chengdu, orphaned in youth, had his gold and jewels registered by the authorities; when Chang surrendered they were carted to court.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞之，令計其直還焉。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor; hearing of it, ordered their value calculated and returned to him.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor, hearing of it, ordered their value calculated and returned to him.

sentences.zh: 玄喆字遵聖，幼聰悟，善隸書。

translations.literal: Xuanzhe; style name Zunsheng; was clever from childhood and skilled in clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzhe, style name Zunsheng, was clever from childhood and skilled in clerical script.

sentences.zh: 年十四，僭封秦王、檢校太尉、同平章事、判六軍諸衛事。

translations.literal: At fourteen he was enfeoffed as King of Qin; honorary Grand Marshal, co-equal councilor, and administrator of the Six Armies and all guards.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he was enfeoffed as King of Qin, honorary Grand Marshal, co-equal councilor, and administrator of the Six Armies and all guards.

sentences.zh: 嚐自書姚崇《口箴》，刻諸石。

translations.literal: He once in his own hand wrote Yao Chong's Mouth Admonition and had it carved on stone.
translations.idiomatic: He once copied Yao Chong's Mouth Admonition in his own hand and had it carved on stone.

sentences.zh: 昶賜以銀器、錦彩。

translations.literal: Chang bestowed on him silver vessels and brocade silks.
translations.idiomatic: Chang rewarded him with silver vessels and brocade silks.

sentences.zh: 廣政二十一年，領武德軍節度。

translations.literal: Guangzheng year twenty-one: he took command of the Wude Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Guangzheng he took command of the Wude Army.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，加兼侍中。

translations.literal: Year twenty-four: additionally made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was additionally made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，立為皇太子。

translations.literal: Year twenty-five: installed as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was installed as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 宋師將至，以玄喆為元帥，精卒萬餘，旌旗用文繡，以錦綢其杠。

translations.literal: When Song forces were about to arrive; Xuanzhe was made commander-in-chief with more than ten thousand picked troops; banners were of figured embroidery and pole shafts were wrapped in brocade silk.
translations.idiomatic: When Song forces were about to arrive, Xuanzhe was made commander-in-chief with more than ten thousand picked troops; banners were of figured embroidery and pole shafts were wrapped in brocade silk.

sentences.zh: 是日微雨，玄喆慮沾濕，令解去。

translations.literal: That day there was light rain; Xuanzhe; fearing they would be soaked; ordered them removed.
translations.idiomatic: That day there was light rain; Xuanzhe, fearing they would be soaked, ordered them removed.

sentences.zh: 俄雨止，復旆之，旌幟數千皆倒係杠上，識者異之。

translations.literal: Soon the rain stopped and they were re-hoisted; several thousand banners and flags all hung upside down on their poles; and those who understood were astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the rain stopped and they were re-hoisted; several thousand banners and flags all hung upside down on their poles, and those who understood were astonished.

sentences.zh: 及聞劍門陷，遂奔東川。

translations.literal: When he heard that Jianmen had fallen; he fled to East River Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that Jianmen had fallen, he fled to East River Circuit.

sentences.zh: 數日，棄軍遁歸。

translations.literal: Within several days he abandoned the army and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Within several days he abandoned the army and fled home.

sentences.zh: 入朝，與昶同日宣製檢校太尉、泰寧軍節度。

translations.literal: On entering court; on the same day as Chang an edict proclaimed him honorary Grand Marshal and military commissioner of the Taining Army.
translations.idiomatic: On entering court, on the same day as Chang an edict proclaimed him honorary Grand Marshal and military commissioner of the Taining Army.

sentences.zh: 昶卒，賜玄喆羊五百口、酒五百壺。

translations.literal: When Chang died; Xuanzhe was granted five hundred sheep and five hundred jars of wine.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang died, Xuanzhe was granted five hundred sheep and five hundred jars of wine.

sentences.zh: 玄喆獻馬二百匹、白玉水晶鞍勒副之。

translations.literal: Xuanzhe presented two hundred horses; white jade and crystal saddle and bridle sets were added.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzhe presented two hundred horses with white jade and crystal saddle and bridle sets.

sentences.zh: 移鎮貝州，在鎮十餘年，亦有治跡。

translations.literal: He was transferred to command at Beizhou and; stationed there more than ten years; also left traces of good governance.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to command at Beizhou and, stationed there more than ten years, also left traces of good governance.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，移鎮定州。

translations.literal: Taiping Xingguo beginning: transferred to Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he was transferred to Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Year third, he was granted the privilege of an independent office equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was granted the privilege of an independent office equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 四年，從平太原，就命為鎮州駐泊兵馬鈐轄。

translations.literal: Year fourth, he followed the pacification of Taiyuan and was appointed on the spot commander of stationed forces at Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he followed the pacification of Taiyuan and was appointed on the spot commander of stationed forces at Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 又從征幽州，率所部攻城之西面。

translations.literal: Again he followed the campaign against Youzhou; leading his division he attacked the city's western face.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed the campaign against Youzhou and led his division to assault the western face of the city.

sentences.zh: 會班師，遣與軍器庫使藥可瓊、深州刺史念金钅巢、左龍武將軍趙延進、殿前都虞候崔翰、四方館使梁迥、翰林使杜彥圭帥兵歸屯定州。

translations.literal: When the army withdrew; he was sent with Armory commissioner Yao Keqiong, Shenzhou prefect Nian Jin'chao, Left Dragon Martial general Zhao Yanjin, Palace Front commander Cui Han, Four Directions Hall commissioner Liang Jiong, and Hanlin commissioner Du Yangui to lead troops back to garrison at Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the army withdrew, he was sent with Armory commissioner Yao Keqiong, Shenzhou prefect Nian Jin'chao, Left Dragon Martial general Zhao Yanjin, Palace Front commander Cui Han, Four Directions Hall commissioner Liang Jiong, and Hanlin commissioner Du Yangui to lead troops back to garrison at Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄契丹入寇，玄喆與諸將校破之徐河。

translations.literal: Soon the Khitans invaded; Xuanzhe and the commanders defeated them at the Xu River.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Khitans invaded; Xuanzhe and the other commanders defeated them at the Xu River.

sentences.zh: 以功封滕國公，入為左龍武軍統軍，判右金吾衛仗。

translations.literal: For his merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Teng; entered court as commander of the Left Dragon Martial Army; and administered the Right Golden Crow Guard regalia.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Teng, entered court as commander of the Left Dragon Martial Army, and administered the Right Golden Crow Guard regalia.

sentences.zh: 未幾，知滑州。

translations.literal: Before long: made prefect of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made prefect of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 淳化初，病，求換瀕淮一小郡養疾。

translations.literal: Chunhua beginning: he fell ill and asked to exchange to a small prefecture on the Huai to nurse illness.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Chunhua he fell ill and asked to be transferred to a small prefecture on the Huai River to convalesce.

sentences.zh: 移知滁州，卒，年五十五。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chuzhou and died there, aged fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Chuzhou and died there, at the age of fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 初，玄喆在貝州，凡民輸稅者皆令出商算，規其餘羨，以備留使之用，人頗苦之。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Xuanzhe was at Beizhou, he required all taxpayers to pay a commercial surcharge and kept the surplus for the expenses of visiting commissioners, to the people's distress.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Xuanzhe was at Beizhou, he required all taxpayers to pay a commercial surcharge and kept the surplus for visiting commissioners' expenses, to the people's distress.

sentences.zh: 景德中，都官員外郎孔揆使河北，表論其事，詔除之。

translations.literal: During Jingde; Ministry of Justice vice director Kong Kui toured Hebei and memorialized on the matter; an edict abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: During Jingde, Ministry of Justice vice director Kong Kui toured Hebei and memorialized on the matter; an edict abolished it.

sentences.zh: 有子十五人：隆記、隆詁、隆說、隆詮，並進士及第。

translations.literal: He had fifteen sons: Longji; Longhe, Longshuo, and Longquan all passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He had fifteen sons: Longji, Longhe, Longshuo, and Longquan all passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 仁贄字忠美，初為左威衛將軍同正。

translations.literal: Renzhi; style name Zhongmei, was first Left Awesome Guard general with concurrent appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Renzhi, style name Zhongmei, was first Left Awesome Guard general with concurrent appointment.

sentences.zh: 廣政十三年，封雅王、檢校太尉。

translations.literal: Guangzheng year thirteen: enfeoffed King of Ya; made honorary Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Guangzheng he was enfeoffed as King of Ya and made honorary Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 二十年，領閬州保寧軍節度。

translations.literal: Year twenty: took command of the Baoning Army at Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he took command of the Baoning Army at Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，加檢校太尉。

translations.literal: Year twenty-four: additionally made honorary Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was additionally made honorary Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 及昶降，遣仁贄奉表詣闕，太祖召見廣德殿，賜襲衣、玉帶、鞍勒馬。

translations.literal: When Chang surrendered; Renzhi was sent to court with the memorial; the Founding Emperor received him in the Guangde Hall and granted court robes; jade belt; and saddled horse.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang surrendered, Renzhi was sent to court with the memorial; the Founding Emperor received him in the Guangde Hall and granted court robes, jade belt, and saddled horse.

sentences.zh: 俄授右神武統軍。

translations.literal: Soon: appointed commander of the Right Divine Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed commander of the Right Divine Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，起復，領大同軍節度、西京都巡檢使。

translations.literal: When his mother's mourning ended he was restored to office; took command of the Datong Army and Western Capital patrol commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother's mourning ended he was restored to office and took command of the Datong Army and the Western Capital patrol commissioner.

sentences.zh: 開寶四年，卒，年四十四，贈太子太師。

translations.literal: Year fourth, of Kaibao he died, aged forty-four, and was posthumously granted Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaibao he died, aged forty-four, and was posthumously granted Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 仁裕字鳴謙，初為左威衛將軍同正，與仁贄同日封彭王、檢校太傅。

translations.literal: Renyu; style name Mingqian; was first Left Awesome Guard general with concurrent appointment and on the same day as Renzhi was enfeoffed as King of Peng and made honorary Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Renyu, style name Mingqian, was first Left Awesome Guard general with concurrent appointment and on the same day as Renzhi was enfeoffed as King of Peng and made honorary Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 廣政二十年，領黔州武泰軍節度。

translations.literal: Guangzheng year twenty: took command of the Wutai Army at Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Guangzheng he took command of the Wutai Army at Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，加檢校太尉。

translations.literal: Year twenty-four: additionally made honorary Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was additionally made honorary Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 歸朝，授檢校太傅、右監門衛上將軍，遷右羽林軍。

translations.literal: On returning to court he was appointed honorary Grand Tutor and senior general of the Right Gate Guard; then transferred to the Right Forest Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he was appointed honorary Grand Tutor and senior general of the Right Gate Guard, then transferred to the Right Forest Guard.

sentences.zh: 開寶三年，卒，年四十四，贈太子太傅。

translations.literal: Year third, of Kaibao he died, aged forty-four, and was posthumously granted Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Kaibao he died, aged forty-four, and was posthumously granted Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 仁操，初為右領軍衛將軍同正，與仁贄同日封嘉王、檢校太傅。

translations.literal: Rencao was first Right Leading Army Guard general with concurrent appointment; on the same day as Renzhi he was enfeoffed King of Jia and made honorary Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Rencao was first Right Leading Army Guard general with concurrent appointment and on the same day as Renzhi was enfeoffed as King of Jia and made honorary Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 廣政二十一年，領果州永寧軍節度。

translations.literal: Guangzheng year twenty-one: took command of the Yongning Army at Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Guangzheng he took command of the Yongning Army at Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 嚐侍昶射於梔子園，仁操連中的者三。

translations.literal: He once attended Chang shooting in the gardenia grove; Rencao three times in succession hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: He once attended Chang shooting in the gardenia grove and Rencao hit the target three times in succession.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，加檢校太尉。

translations.literal: Year twenty-four: additionally made honorary Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was additionally made honorary Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 尤奉釋氏，深究其理。

translations.literal: He especially revered the Buddhist teaching and deeply investigated its principles.
translations.idiomatic: He especially revered Buddhism and studied its principles deeply.

sentences.zh: 歸朝，授右監門衛上將軍，累遷右龍武統軍。

translations.literal: On returning to court he was appointed senior general of the Right Gate Guard; repeatedly promoted to commander of the Right Dragon Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he was appointed senior general of the Right Gate Guard and was repeatedly promoted to commander of the Right Dragon Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，卒。

translations.literal: Year third, of Yongxi he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxi he died.

sentences.zh: 伊審征字申圖，并州人。

translations.literal: Yi Shenzheng; style name Shentu, was a man of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Shenzheng, style name Shentu, was a man of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父延瑰，隨知祥入蜀。

translations.literal: Father Yan'gui followed Zhixiang in entering Shu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan'gui followed Zhixiang into Shu.

sentences.zh: 知祥僭位，以女妻延瑰，僭封崇華公主。

translations.literal: When Zhixiang assumed the imperial title he gave his daughter in marriage to Yan'gui; posthumously enfeoffed Princess Chonghua.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhixiang assumed the imperial title he gave his daughter in marriage to Yan'gui and enfeoffed her as Princess Chonghua.

sentences.zh: 延瑰曆陵、嘉、眉三州刺史。

translations.literal: Yan'gui successively served as prefect of Ling, Jia, and Mei.
translations.idiomatic: Yan'gui served successively as prefect of Ling, Jia, and Mei.

sentences.zh: 審征幼以孝聞，母病，割股肉啖之。

translations.literal: Shenzheng from childhood was known for filial piety; when his mother was ill he cut thigh flesh for her to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzheng was known for filial piety from childhood; when his mother fell ill he cut flesh from his thigh for her to eat.

sentences.zh: 以父任，曆蜀州刺史、雲安榷鹽使。
