translations.literal: By his father's office he served as Shu prefect and Yun'an salt monopoly commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's position he served as prefect of Shu and salt monopoly commissioner of Yun'an.

sentences.zh: 廣政十四年，高延昭求解機務，急召為通奏使、知樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Guangzheng; when Gao Yanzhao asked to be relieved of state affairs; Shenzheng was urgently summoned as memorial courier and privy councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Guangzheng, when Gao Yanzhao asked to be relieved of state affairs, Shenzheng was urgently summoned as memorial courier and privy councilor.

sentences.zh: 久之，領蜀州刺史。

translations.literal: After a long time he took office as prefect of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he took command as prefect of Shu.

sentences.zh: 秦、鳳興師，命檢校城砦，俄領武泰軍節度。

translations.literal: When Qin and Feng raised armies he was ordered to inspect fortifications; soon he took command of the Wutai Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin and Feng came under attack he was ordered to inspect fortifications and soon took command of the Wutai Army.

sentences.zh: 選其子崇度尚公主。

translations.literal: His son Chongdu was chosen to marry the princess.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chongdu was chosen to marry a princess.

sentences.zh: 又改寧江軍節度、同平章事，與王昭遠俱掌機務。

translations.literal: He was then transferred to military commissioner of the Ningjiang Army and co-equal councilor; sharing state secrets with Wang Zhaoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to military commissioner of the Ningjiang Army and co-equal councilor, sharing state secrets with Wang Zhaoyuan.

sentences.zh: 昶事無大小，一以谘之。

translations.literal: In matters large and small Chang consulted him on everything.
translations.idiomatic: In all matters large and small Chang consulted him.

sentences.zh: 常自以康濟經略為己任。

translations.literal: He often took healing the state and grand strategy as his own responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: He often took healing the state and grand strategy as his own duty.

sentences.zh: 屬宋師入境，審征首奉降表詣軍前。

translations.literal: When Song armies entered the border; Shenzheng was the first to present a surrender petition at the army front.
translations.idiomatic: When Song armies entered the border, Shenzheng was the first to present a surrender petition at the army front.

sentences.zh: 昭遠時統軍，敗走。

translations.literal: Zhaoyuan was then commanding the army; defeated, he fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyuan was then commanding the army and fled in defeat.

sentences.zh: 時人笑之。

translations.literal: People of the time laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time laughed at this.

sentences.zh: 審征歸朝，授靜難軍節度。

translations.literal: When Shenzheng returned to court he was made military commissioner of the Jingnan Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzheng returned to court he was appointed military commissioner of the Jingnan Army.

sentences.zh: 乾德六年，移鎮延安。

translations.literal: Year sixth, of Qiande he was transferred to Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Qiande he was transferred to Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 開寶末入朝，改右屯衛上將軍。

translations.literal: Kaibao end: entered court; made senior general of the Right Garrison Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Kaibao he entered court and was made senior general of the Right Garrison Guard.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，判右金吾衛仗。

translations.literal: Year second, of Taiping Xingguo he administered the Right Golden Crow Guard regalia.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he administered the Right Golden Crow Guard regalia.

sentences.zh: 雍熙五年，卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongxi he died, aged seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yongxi he died, at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 韓保正，字永吉，潞州長子人。

translations.literal: Han Baozheng; style name Yongji; was a man of Changzi in Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Han Baozheng, style name Yongji, was a man of Changzi in Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 父昭運，從知祥入蜀。

translations.literal: Father Zhaoyun followed Zhixiang in entering Shu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhaoyun followed Zhixiang into Shu.

sentences.zh: 及知祥僭號，署珍州刺史。

translations.literal: When Zhixiang assumed the imperial title, he appointed him prefect of Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhixiang took the throne, he appointed him prefect of Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 保正初事知祥為押衙，及僭位，以為豐德庫使兼廣義庫使、眉州刺史、樞密副使。

translations.literal: Baozheng first served Zhixiang as escort commander; when he assumed the imperial title, Baozheng was made commissioner of the Fengde Treasury, concurrent commissioner of the Guangyi Treasury, prefect of Meizhou, and deputy privy councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Baozheng first served Zhixiang as escort commander; when he took the throne, Baozheng was made commissioner of the Fengde Treasury, concurrent commissioner of the Guangyi Treasury, prefect of Meizhou, and deputy privy councilor.

sentences.zh: 復刺漢州，拜宣徽北院使。

translations.literal: Again made prefect of Hanzhou; appointed commissioner of the Northern Court of the Xuanhui Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made prefect of Hanzhou and appointed commissioner of the Northern Court of the Xuanhui Bureau.

sentences.zh: 會鳳翔侯益歸款，以保正為北路行營都監，以圖岐陽。

translations.literal: When Hou Yi of Fengxiang submitted; Baozheng was made army inspector of the northern route forward camp to take Qiyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Yi of Fengxiang submitted, Baozheng was made army inspector of the northern route forward camp to take Qiyang.

sentences.zh: 時晉昌趙讚亦謀歸蜀，為王景崇所逼，棄城東奔。

translations.literal: At that time Zhao Zan of Jinchang also plotted to submit to Shu but; pressed by Wang Jingchong; abandoned the city and fled east.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhao Zan of Jinchang also plotted to submit to Shu but, pressed by Wang Jingchong, abandoned the city and fled east.

sentences.zh: 偽將李廷珪先退師，保正次陳倉，與大將張虔釗、龐福誠謀議不葉，益亦中變，遂還成都。

translations.literal: The false general Li Tinggui withdrew first; Baozheng halted at Chencang; with grand generals Zhang Qianzhao and Pang Fucheng his counsel did not agree; Yi also changed mid-course; and they returned to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: The false general Li Tinggui withdrew first; Baozheng halted at Chencang; with grand generals Zhang Qianzhao and Pang Fucheng his counsel did not agree; Yi also changed mid-course, and they returned to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 俄為雄武節度，領兵出新關，至隴州，漢兵固守，保正無功而還。

translations.literal: Soon he was made military commissioner of the Xiongwu Army; led troops out through Xin Pass to Longzhou; Han troops held firm and Baozheng returned without success.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made military commissioner of the Xiongwu Army, led troops out through Xin Pass to Longzhou; Han troops held firm and Baozheng returned without success.

sentences.zh: 復屯雄武。

translations.literal: Again he garrisoned at Xiongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He again garrisoned at Xiongwu.

sentences.zh: 廣政十四年，赴成都，其親吏楊虔範訟保正不法，昶令斬虔範，釋保正不問。

translations.literal: Guangzheng year fourteen: he went to Chengdu; his personal clerk Yang Qianfan sued Baozheng for misconduct; Chang ordered Qianfan beheaded and released Baozheng without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Guangzheng he went to Chengdu; his personal clerk Yang Qianfan sued Baozheng for misconduct; Chang ordered Qianfan executed and released Baozheng without inquiry.

sentences.zh: 俄改夔州寧江軍節度。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to military commissioner of the Ningjiang Army at Kuizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to military commissioner of the Ningjiang Army at Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 李昊讓度支，以保正代之。

translations.literal: Li Hao yielded the revenue commission; Baozheng replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hao yielded the revenue commission and Baozheng replaced him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，加宣徽南院使、山南節度、左衛聖步軍節度指揮使，遷奉鸞肅衛馬步軍都指揮使，又選其子崇遂尚主。

translations.literal: Before long he was additionally made commissioner of the Southern Court of the Xuanhui Bureau; Shannan military commissioner; and commander of the Left Guard Sacred infantry; he was promoted to commander of the Fengluan Solitary Guard horse-and-foot army; and his son Chongsui was chosen to marry a princess.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was additionally made commissioner of the Southern Court of the Xuanhui Bureau, Shannan military commissioner, and commander of the Left Guard Sacred infantry; he was promoted to commander of the Fengluan Solitary Guard horse-and-foot army, and his son Chongsui was chosen to marry a princess.

sentences.zh: 宋初，荊南高繼衝納土，昶聞之，以保正為峽路都指揮製置使，屯夔州，以經畫邊事。

translations.literal: Early in Song; when Gao Jichong of Jingnan surrendered his territory; Chang heard of it and made Baozheng overall commander and commissioner for the Gorges route; garrisoning at Kuizhou to manage frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Song, when Gao Jichong of Jingnan surrendered his territory, Chang heard of it and made Baozheng overall commander and commissioner for the Gorges route, garrisoning at Kuizhou to manage frontier affairs.

sentences.zh: 遷檢校太尉兼侍中。

translations.literal: Promoted to honorary Grand Marshal and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to honorary Grand Marshal and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 聞太祖將加兵，以保正為山南節度、興元武定緣邊諸砦屯駐都指揮使。

translations.literal: Hearing that the Founding Emperor was about to send troops; Chang made Baozheng Shannan military commissioner and overall commander of garrisons along the Xingyuan, Wuding, and frontier forts.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that the Founding Emperor was about to send troops, Chang made Baozheng Shannan military commissioner and overall commander of garrisons along the Xingyuan, Wuding, and frontier forts.

sentences.zh: 及王全斌至，保正棄興元，保西縣。

translations.literal: When Wang Quanbin arrived; Baozheng abandoned Xingyuan and held Xixian.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Quanbin arrived, Baozheng abandoned Xingyuan and held Xixian.

sentences.zh: 王師進圍之，保正懦懼不敢出，遣人依山背城結陣以自固，為史延德所破。

translations.literal: The royal army advanced to besiege him; Baozheng was timid and afraid to come out; sent men to form a battle line along the mountain backing the city to secure himself; and was defeated by Shi Yande.
translations.idiomatic: The royal army advanced to besiege him; Baozheng was timid and afraid to come out, sent men to form a battle line along the mountain backing the city to secure himself, and was defeated by Shi Yande.

sentences.zh: 保正以麾下遁，延德追擒之，送全斌。

translations.literal: Baozheng fled with his followers; Yande pursued, captured him, and sent him to Quanbin.
translations.idiomatic: Baozheng fled with his followers; Yande pursued and captured him and sent him to Quanbin.

sentences.zh: 全斌驛置闕下，太祖召升殿勞問，賜袍笏、金帶、茵褥、鞍勒馬，仍賜甲第。

translations.literal: Quanbin sent him by post relay to court; the Founding Emperor summoned him to the hall; consoled him; and granted robe and court tablet; gold belt, bedding, saddled horse, and also a fine residence.
translations.idiomatic: Quanbin sent him by post relay to court; the Founding Emperor summoned him to the hall, consoled him, and granted robe and court tablet, gold belt, bedding, saddled horse, and also a fine residence.

sentences.zh: 未及命官而卒，贈右千牛衛上將軍。

translations.literal: Before an office could be conferred he died; posthumously granted senior general of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Before an office could be conferred he died and was posthumously granted senior general of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard.

sentences.zh: 王昭遠，益州成都人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhaoyuan was a man of Chengdu, Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhaoyuan was a man of Chengdu in Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 幼孤貧。

translations.literal: Orphaned and poor in youth.
translations.idiomatic: He was orphaned and poor in youth.

sentences.zh: 年十三，依東郭僧智諲為童子。

translations.literal: At age thirteen he attached himself to the monk Zhijin of the eastern quarter as a temple boy.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he attached himself to the monk Zhijin of the eastern quarter as a temple boy.

sentences.zh: 知祥鎮蜀，一日飯僧於府署，昭遠持巾履從智諲，得入。

translations.literal: When Zhixiang governed Shu; one day he fed monks at the government office; Zhaoyuan carried towel and shoes for Zhijin and was able to enter.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhixiang governed Shu, one day he fed monks at the government office; Zhaoyuan carried towel and shoes for Zhijin and was able to enter.

sentences.zh: 時昶方就學，知祥見昭遠聰慧，留給事昶左右。

translations.literal: Chang was then beginning studies; Zhixiang saw Zhaoyuan was clever and kept him to serve at Chang's side.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was then beginning his studies; Zhixiang saw that Zhaoyuan was clever and kept him to serve at Chang's side.

sentences.zh: 昶嗣位，以昭遠為卷簾使、茶酒庫使。

translations.literal: When Chang succeeded; he made Zhaoyuan curtain-lifting attendant and commissioner of the tea and wine treasury.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang succeeded, he made Zhaoyuan curtain-lifting attendant and commissioner of the tea and wine treasury.

sentences.zh: 會樞密使王處回出知梓州，昶以樞密事權太重，乃以昭遠及普豐庫使高延昭為通奏使、知樞密院事，機務一以委之，府庫財帛恣其取不問。

translations.literal: When privy councilor Wang Chuhui went out to govern Zizhou; Chang felt that privy affairs carried too much weight and therefore made Zhaoyuan and Pufeng Treasury commissioner Gao Yanzhao memorial couriers and privy councilors; entrusting all state secrets to them and letting them take from the treasuries without question.
translations.idiomatic: When privy councilor Wang Chuhui went out to govern Zizhou, Chang felt that privy affairs carried too much weight and therefore made Zhaoyuan and Pufeng Treasury commissioner Gao Yanzhao memorial couriers and privy councilors, entrusting all state secrets to them and letting them take from the treasuries without question.

sentences.zh: 加領眉州刺史，出為永平軍節度。

translations.literal: Additionally made prefect of Meizhou; sent out as military commissioner of the Yongping Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally made prefect of Meizhou and sent out as military commissioner of the Yongping Army.

sentences.zh: 不數月，會昭武李繼勳以目疾不能視事，議以閑地處之，昭遠遽以永平讓繼勳。

translations.literal: Within several months; when Li Jixun of Zhaowu could not govern because of eye disease and it was proposed to place him in an idle post; Zhaoyuan hastily yielded Yongping to Jixun.
translations.idiomatic: Within several months, when Li Jixun of Zhaowu could not govern because of eye disease and it was proposed to place him in an idle post, Zhaoyuan hastily yielded Yongping to Jixun.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，為夔州寧江軍節度。

translations.literal: After more than a year: made military commissioner of the Ningjiang Army at Kuizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was made military commissioner of the Ningjiang Army at Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 昶母常言昭遠不可用，昶不從。

translations.literal: Chang's mother often said Zhaoyuan could not be used; Chang did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's mother often said Zhaoyuan should not be used; Chang did not listen.

sentences.zh: 未幾，兼領山南西道節度、同平章事。

translations.literal: Before long he additionally held Shannan West Circuit military commissioner and co-equal councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he additionally took Shannan West Circuit military commissioner and co-equal councilor.

sentences.zh: 及入謝，求解通奏職，遂以左街使張仁貴為副使、知樞密以代之。

translations.literal: When he came in to give thanks he asked to be relieved of the memorial courier post; Zhang Rengui of the Left Street was made deputy and acting privy councilor in his place.
translations.idiomatic: When he came in to give thanks he asked to be relieved of the memorial courier post; Zhang Rengui of the Left Street was made deputy and privy councilor in his place.

sentences.zh: 昭遠好讀兵書，頗以方略自許。

translations.literal: Zhaoyuan loved reading military books and considerably prided himself on strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyuan loved reading military books and prided himself considerably on strategy.

sentences.zh: 宋師入境，昶遣昭遠與趙崇韜率兵拒戰。

translations.literal: When Song armies entered the border; Chang sent Zhaoyuan and Zhao Chongtao to lead troops in resistance.
translations.idiomatic: When Song armies entered the border, Chang sent Zhaoyuan and Zhao Chongtao to lead troops in resistance.

sentences.zh: 始發成都，昶遣其宰相李昊等餞郊外。

translations.literal: As they set out from Chengdu; Chang sent his chief councilor Li Hao and others to farewell them in the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: As they set out from Chengdu, Chang sent his chief councilor Li Hao and others to farewell them in the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 昭遠酒酣，攘臂曰：“是行也，非止克敵，當領此二三萬雕麵惡少兒，取中原如反掌耳。”

translations.literal: Zhaoyuan; flushed with wine; rolled up his sleeves and said: "On this campaign we will not merely defeat the enemy—we shall lead these twenty or thirty thousand painted-face ruffians and take the central plain as easily as turning the hand."
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyuan, flushed with wine, rolled up his sleeves and said: "On this campaign we will not merely defeat the enemy—we shall lead these twenty or thirty thousand painted-face ruffians and take the central plain as easily as turning the hand."

sentences.zh: 及行，執鐵如意指麾軍事，自方諸葛亮。

translations.literal: When they marched he held an iron ruyi scepter to direct military affairs; he compared himself to Zhuge Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When they marched he held an iron ruyi scepter to direct military affairs and compared himself to Zhuge Liang.

sentences.zh: 將至漢源，聞劍門已破，昭遠股栗，發言失次。

translations.literal: When they were about to reach Hanyuan and heard that Jianmen had fallen; Zhaoyuan's legs trembled and his speech lost order.
translations.idiomatic: When they were about to reach Hanyuan and heard that Jianmen had fallen, Zhaoyuan's legs trembled and his speech lost order.

sentences.zh: 崇韜布陣將戰，昭遠據胡床，皇恐不能起。

translations.literal: Chongtao deployed the battle line to fight; Zhaoyuan sat on a folding chair; too terrified to rise.
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao deployed the battle line to fight; Zhaoyuan sat on a folding chair, too terrified to rise.

sentences.zh: 俄崇韜敗，乃免胄棄甲走投東川，匿倉舍下，悲嗟流涕，目盡腫，惟誦羅隱詩云：“運去英雄不自由。”

translations.literal: Soon Chongtao was defeated; Zhaoyuan doffed helmet and cast off armor and fled toward East River Circuit; hiding under a granary shed; sighing and weeping until his eyes swelled shut; reciting only Luo Yin's poem: "When fortune departs; even heroes are not free."
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chongtao was defeated; Zhaoyuan doffed helmet and cast off armor and fled toward East River Circuit, hiding under a granary shed, sighing and weeping until his eyes swelled shut, reciting only Luo Yin's poem: "When fortune departs, even heroes are not free."

sentences.zh: 俄為追騎所執，送闕下，太祖釋之，授左領軍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Soon pursuing horsemen seized him and sent him to court; the Founding Emperor released him and appointed him grand general of the Left Leading Army Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was seized by pursuing horsemen and sent to court; the Founding Emperor released him and appointed him grand general of the Left Leading Army Guard.

sentences.zh: 廣南平，奉使交阯。

translations.literal: When Guangnan was pacified he was dispatched as envoy to Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangnan was pacified he was sent as envoy to Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 開寶八年，卒。

translations.literal: Year eighth, of Kaibao he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Kaibao he died.

sentences.zh: 趙崇韜，并州太原人。

translations.literal: Zhao Chongtao was a man of Taiyuan, Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chongtao was a man of Taiyuan in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父廷隱，隨知祥入蜀。

translations.literal: Father Tingyin followed Zhixiang in entering Shu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tingyin followed Zhixiang into Shu.

sentences.zh: 廷隱拳勇有智略，知祥麾下無及者。

translations.literal: Tingyin was brave in boxing and wise in strategy; none under Zhixiang matched him.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyin was brave in combat and resourceful in strategy; none under Zhixiang matched him.

sentences.zh: 東川董璋襲成都，廷隱大破之。

translations.literal: When Dong Zhang of East River Circuit attacked Chengdu; Tingyin routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Zhang of East River Circuit attacked Chengdu, Tingyin routed him utterly.

sentences.zh: 璋奔歸，為部下所殺，知祥遂有其地。

translations.literal: Zhang fled back; his subordinates killed him; Zhixiang then possessed his territory.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang fled back and was killed by his subordinates; Zhixiang then possessed his territory.

sentences.zh: 及僭號，以廷隱總親軍，為衛聖諸軍馬步軍指揮使，累遷至太師、中書令、宋王。

translations.literal: When he assumed the imperial title, he made Tingyin commander of the personal army, appointed him Commander of the Horse and Foot Forces of the Imperial Guard Armies, and promoted him repeatedly until Grand Preceptor, Director of the Secretariat, and Prince of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhixiang had taken the imperial title, he put Tingyin in command of the personal army as Commander of the Horse and Foot Forces of the Imperial Guard Armies, promoting him in time to Grand Preceptor, Director of the Secretariat, and Prince of Song.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡忠武。

translations.literal: When he died, he was given the posthumous title Loyal and Martial.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled Loyal and Martial.

sentences.zh: 崇韜驍果有父風。

translations.literal: Chongtao was fierce and resolute and had his father's mettle.
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao was bold and resolute—a true son of his father.

sentences.zh: 昶自置殿直四番，取將家及死事孤子為之，始命李仁罕子繼宏、趙季良子元振、張知業子繼昭、侯洪實子令欽及崇韜，分為都知領之。

translations.literal: Chang himself established four rotations of Palace Directs, drawn from generals' families and orphans of men who died in service; he first appointed Li Jihong son of Renhan, Zhao Yuanzhen son of Jiliang, Zhang Jizhao son of Zhiye, Hou Lingqin son of Hongshi, and Chongtao, each as a command chief to lead them.
translations.idiomatic: Chang personally set up four rotations of Palace Directs, selecting sons of generals' houses and orphans of men who had died in service. He first appointed Li Renhan's son Jihong, Zhao Jiliang's son Yuanzhen, Zhang Zhiye's son Jizhao, Hou Hongshi's son Lingqin, and Chongtao, each to serve as a command chief over one rotation.

sentences.zh: 後累遷至客省使。

translations.literal: Later he was promoted repeatedly to Guest Reception Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted step by step to Guest Reception Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 周世宗克秦、鳳，將入蜀境，為崇韜拒退。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong of Later Zhou took Qin and Feng and was about to enter Shu territory, Chongtao repelled him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong of Later Zhou captured Qin and Feng and was poised to cross into Shu, Chongtao drove him back.

sentences.zh: 曆左右衛聖步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: He served in turn as Commander of the Left and Right Imperial Guard Foot Forces.
translations.idiomatic: He held the posts of Commander of the Left and Right Imperial Guard Foot Forces in succession.

sentences.zh: 選其子文亮尚公主。

translations.literal: His son Wenliang was chosen to marry a princess.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wenliang was selected to marry an imperial princess.

sentences.zh: 加領洋州武定軍節度、山南武定緣邊諸砦都指揮副使。

translations.literal: He was further made Military Commissioner of the Wuding Army at Yang Prefecture and Deputy Commander of the Border Forts of the Wuding Army on the Southern Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally appointed Military Commissioner of the Wuding Army at Yang Prefecture and Deputy Commander of the Wuding Army's border forts along the southern mountains.

sentences.zh: 漢源之戰，獨策馬先登，及蜀軍敗，猶手擊殺十數人，為宋師所擒。

translations.literal: At the battle of Hanyuan he alone spurred his horse to lead the charge; when the Shu army was defeated he still slew a dozen or more men by hand before being captured by the Song forces.
translations.idiomatic: At Hanyuan he alone charged ahead on horseback; even after the Shu army was routed he killed more than ten men with his own hands before Song troops seized him.

sentences.zh: 高彥儔，并州太原人。

translations.literal: Gao Yanchou was a man of Taiyuan in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yanchou came from Taiyuan in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父暉，宣威軍使。

translations.literal: His father Hui was Military Commissioner of the Xuanwei Army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hui had been military commissioner of the Xuanwei Army.

sentences.zh: 彥儔從知祥入蜀，累曆軍校，為昭武軍監押。

translations.literal: Yanchou followed Zhixiang into Shu, rose through military ranks, and became Supervisory Commissioner of the Zhaowu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchou followed Zhixiang into Shu, advanced through the military grades, and became supervisory commissioner of the Zhaowu Army.

sentences.zh: 昶嗣位，遷邛州刺史，改馬步軍使。

translations.literal: When Chang succeeded to the throne, Yanchou was transferred to Prefect of Qiong Prefecture and changed to Horse and Foot Forces Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang took the throne, Yanchou was moved to prefect of Qiong Prefecture and reassigned as commissioner of horse and foot forces.

sentences.zh: 會漢兵入大散關，克安都砦，彥儔以所部先進。

translations.literal: When Han troops entered Dasanguan and captured Andu Fort, Yanchou led his division forward first.
translations.idiomatic: Han forces entered Dasanguan and took Andu Fort; Yanchou led his command forward in the van.

sentences.zh: 漢人燒砦毀閣遁去，彥儔盡銳追之，復其砦而還。

translations.literal: The Han men burned the fort, destroyed the pass structures, and fled; Yanchou pursued with all his best troops, recovered the fort, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Han troops burned the fort, wrecked the pass works, and fled; Yanchou pursued with his finest troops, retook the fort, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 未幾，彥儔領趙州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long Yanchou was made Prefect of Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made prefect of Zhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 俄為奉鑾肅衛都指揮副使，改右驍銳馬軍都指揮使，加光聖馬軍都指揮使，真拜源州武定軍節度。

translations.literal: Soon he became Deputy Commander of the Imperial Escort and Ceremonial Guard, then changed to Commander of the Right Swift and Sharp Horse Forces, added Commander of the Bright Sage Horse Forces, and was formally appointed Military Commissioner of the Wuding Army at Yuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after he became deputy commander of the Imperial Escort and Ceremonial Guard, then commander of the Right Swift and Sharp Horse Forces, with an added post as commander of the Bright Sage Horse Forces, and finally received formal appointment as military commissioner of the Wuding Army at Yuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 周顯德初，向訓攻鳳州，昶令彥儔出兵解圍。

translations.literal: In the early Xiande era, Xiang Xun attacked Feng Prefecture; Chang ordered Yanchou to lead troops to lift the siege.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiande reign, Xiang Xun besieged Feng Prefecture, and Chang ordered Yanchou out to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 未至，聞敗軍於唐倉，因潰歸。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, he heard that the army had been defeated at Tangcang, and his force collapsed and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could arrive he learned that the army had been beaten at Tangcang, and his troops broke and fled home.

sentences.zh: 判官趙比閉關不納，以城歸朝廷。

translations.literal: Prefectural aide Zhao Bi closed the gates and would not admit them, surrendering the city to the court.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural aide Zhao Bi shut the gates against them and surrendered the city to the Song court.

sentences.zh: 彥儔遁歸成都，昶不之罪，以為右奉鑾肅衛都指揮使，改功德使。

translations.literal: Yanchou fled back to Chengdu; Chang did not punish him and made him Commander of the Right Imperial Escort and Ceremonial Guard, then changed him to Merit Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchou escaped to Chengdu; Chang did not blame him, appointing him commander of the Right Imperial Escort and Ceremonial Guard and later making him merit commissioner.

sentences.zh: 廣政二十二年，出授夔州寧江軍都巡檢製置、招討使，加宣徽北院事、利州昭武軍節度。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Guangzheng he was sent out as Commander and Pacification Commissioner of the Ningjiang Army at Qia Prefecture, Director of the Northern Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat, and Military Commissioner of the Zhaowu Army at Li Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Guangzheng he was posted out as commander, pacification commissioner, and suppression commissioner of the Ningjiang Army at Qia Prefecture, with added titles as director of the northern bureau of the Imperial Secretariat and military commissioner of the Zhaowu Army at Li Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及宋師至，彥儔謂副使趙崇濟、監軍武守謙曰：“北軍涉遠而來，利在速戰，不如堅壁以待之。”

translations.literal: When Song forces arrived, Yanchou said to Deputy Commissioner Zhao Chongji and Supervisory Commissioner Wu Shouqian: "The northern army has come from afar; their advantage lies in a swift battle—we would do better to hold the walls and wait them out."
translations.idiomatic: When Song troops arrived, Yanchou told Deputy Commissioner Zhao Chongji and Supervisory Commissioner Wu Shouqian, "The northern army has marched far; they profit from a quick fight. We should hold the walls and wear them down."

sentences.zh: 守謙不從，獨領麾下以出。

translations.literal: Shouqian would not agree and led his own troops out alone.
translations.idiomatic: Shouqian refused to listen and marched out with only his own men.

sentences.zh: 時大將劉廷讓頓兵白帝廟西，遣騎將張廷翰等引兵與守謙戰豬頭鋪，守謙敗走。

translations.literal: At that time the great general Liu Tingrang had encamped west of Baidi Temple and sent cavalry generals Zhang Tinghan and others to meet Shouqian in battle at Zhutoupu; Shouqian was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Song commander Liu Tingrang was then encamped west of Baidi Temple; he sent cavalry generals Zhang Tinghan and others to fight Shouqian at Zhutoupu, and Shouqian was routed.

sentences.zh: 廷翰等乘勝登其城，廷讓率大軍繼至。

translations.literal: Tinghan and the others pressed their victory to scale the city walls, and Tingrang led the main army up after them.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghan and his men pressed the victory and scaled the walls; Tingrang followed with the main army.

sentences.zh: 彥儔以所部將出拒戰，宋師已乘城而入。

translations.literal: Yanchou was about to lead his division out to resist when Song troops had already scaled the walls and entered.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchou was preparing to lead his troops out to fight when Song soldiers were already over the walls and inside the city.

sentences.zh: 彥儔惶駭失次，不知計所出。

translations.literal: Yanchou was panic-stricken and at a loss, not knowing what plan to adopt.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchou was terrified and disordered, with no plan left to him.

sentences.zh: 判官羅濟勸令單騎歸成都，彥儔曰：“我昔已失天水，今復不能守夔州，縱不忍殺我，亦何面目見蜀人哉！”

translations.literal: Aide Luo Ji urged him to return alone on horseback to Chengdu; Yanchou said: "I once already lost Tianshui; now I cannot hold Qia Prefecture either—even if they spare my life, what face have I to show the people of Shu?"
translations.idiomatic: His aide Luo Ji urged him to ride alone back to Chengdu. Yanchou said, "I already lost Tianshui once; now I cannot hold Qia Prefecture. Even if they spare me, what face can I show the people of Shu?"

sentences.zh: 濟又勸其降，彥儔曰：“老幼百口在成都，若一身偷生，舉族何負？

translations.literal: Ji again urged him to surrender; Yanchou said: "Old and young, a hundred mouths are in Chengdu—if I alone steal life, what burden for my whole clan?"
translations.idiomatic: Ji then urged him to surrender. Yanchou said, "A hundred of my kin, old and young, are in Chengdu. If I alone save myself, what becomes of my whole family?"

sentences.zh: 吾今日止有死耳！”

translations.literal: Today I have only death!"
translations.idiomatic: Today death is all that is left for me!"

sentences.zh: 即解符印授濟，具衣冠望西北再拜，登樓縱火自焚。

translations.literal: He at once handed over his seals and tallies to Ji, donned full court dress, bowed twice toward the northwest, ascended a tower, set fire, and burned himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately gave his seals and tallies to Ji, put on full court dress, bowed twice toward the northwest, climbed a tower, set it ablaze, and burned himself alive.

sentences.zh: 後數日，廷讓得其骨煨燼中，以禮收葬。

translations.literal: Several days later Tingrang found his bones in the ashes and buried them with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Days later Tingrang recovered his bones from the embers and buried him with full rites.

sentences.zh: 初，昶母語昶“惟彥儔可任”，及是，果能死難。

translations.literal: Earlier Chang's mother had told Chang "only Yanchou can be entrusted"; at this he indeed died for the cause.
translations.idiomatic: Long before, Chang's mother had told him, "Only Yanchou can be relied upon"—and now he proved able to die for the realm.

sentences.zh: 趙彥韜，興州順政人，為本州義軍裨校。

translations.literal: Zhao Yantao was a man of Shunzheng in Xing Prefecture, a deputy commander of the righteous army of his native prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yantao was from Shunzheng in Xing Prefecture and served as a deputy commander of the local righteous army.

sentences.zh: 乾德中，昶遣與興國軍討擊使孫遇及楊蠲為諜至都下，彥韜潛取昶與并州蠟丸帛書以告，因言伐蜀之狀。

translations.literal: In the Qiande era Chang sent him with the Pacification Commissioner of the Xingguo Army Sun Yu and Yang Juan as spies to the capital; Yantao secretly took the wax-ball silk letter from Chang to Bingzhou and disclosed it, also reporting the situation for attacking Shu.
translations.idiomatic: During Qiande, Chang sent him with Sun Yu, pacification commissioner of the Xingguo Army, and Yang Juan as spies to the capital. Yantao secretly seized the wax-sealed silk message from Chang to Bing Prefecture and turned it in, describing as well the conditions for an attack on Shu.

sentences.zh: 太祖並赦遇、蠲，出師西討，並以為鄉導。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor pardoned Yu and Juan alike, launched a western campaign, and made them both guides.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor pardoned both Yu and Juan, marched west to attack Shu, and employed them as local guides.

sentences.zh: 克興州，以為本州馬步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: When Xing Prefecture was taken, Yantao was made Commander of the Horse and Foot Forces of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After Xing Prefecture fell he was made commander of its horse and foot forces.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，遷本州刺史，移澧州。

translations.literal: After Shu was pacified he was promoted to Prefect of his native prefecture, then transferred to Li Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu was pacified he was promoted to prefect of his home prefecture, then transferred to Li Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 性凶率，所為不法，部民有訴被盜劫財物，鞫之不實，彥韜手殺之，探取其心肝。

translations.literal: By nature he was fierce and reckless; his conduct was unlawful. When subjects complained of robbery of their property, the inquiry found the charge untrue, yet Yantao killed the man with his own hand and plucked out heart and liver.
translations.idiomatic: He was brutal by nature and acted outside the law. When a subject complained of robbery, the investigation found no crime—yet Yantao killed the man himself and tore out his heart and liver.

sentences.zh: 民家詣闕訴冤，太祖怒，令杖配蔡州。

translations.literal: The household went to the palace to plead their wrong; the Founding Emperor was angry and ordered him beaten and exiled to Cai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The family went to court to plead their grievance; the Founding Emperor was furious and had Yantao beaten and banished to Cai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 龍景昭，夔州奉節人。

translations.literal: Long Jingzhao was a man of Fengjie in Qia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Long Jingzhao was a native of Fengjie in Qia Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少有武勇，事蜀為義軍裨校，以功遷戰棹都將。

translations.literal: In youth he had martial courage; he served Shu as a righteous-army deputy commander and was promoted for merit to Battle Raft Director.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he showed martial courage; he served Shu as a righteous-army deputy commander and, for merit, was promoted to battle-raft director.

sentences.zh: 久之，擢為施州刺史。

translations.literal: After a long while he was promoted to Prefect of Shi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was elevated to prefect of Shi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 乾德中，諸將伐蜀，分兵由峽路入，將壓其境。

translations.literal: In the Qiande era the generals attacked Shu; they divided forces to enter by the gorge route and were about to press the border.
translations.idiomatic: During Qiande the generals invaded Shu, sending columns through the gorges to press upon its territory.

sentences.zh: 景昭率官吏以牛酒犒宋師，迎入城。

translations.literal: Jingzhao led officials with cattle and wine to feast the Song army and welcomed them into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao led his officials out with cattle and wine to feast the Song army and welcomed them into the city.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞之，甚悅。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor heard of it and was very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor heard of this he was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，即授永州刺史。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified he was immediately appointed Prefect of Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shu was pacified he was promptly appointed prefect of Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 秩滿入朝，改右千牛衛將軍。

translations.literal: When his term expired he came to court and was made General of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he came to court and was made a general of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard.

sentences.zh: 開寶三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaibao he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Kaibao.

sentences.zh: 昶之入朝也，為左羽林將軍、景昭弟處瑭等四人隨行，卒於道。

translations.literal: When Chang went to the capital, Chutang—Jingzhao's younger brother—and three others, who were Left Feathered Forest generals, accompanied him and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang went to court, Jingzhao's younger brother Chutang and three other Left Feathered Forest generals accompanied him and died on the journey.

sentences.zh: 太祖憫之，以其男補供奉官殿直。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor pitied them and appointed their sons Palace Attendant Directs.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor took pity on them and appointed their sons as palace attendant directs.

sentences.zh: 幸寅遜，蜀人。

translations.literal: Xing Yinxun was a man of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Yinxun was a native of Shu.

sentences.zh: 初仕昶為茂州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: He first served Chang as Recorder of Ma Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered Chang's service as recorder of Ma Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 昶好擊球，雖盛暑不已。

translations.literal: Chang loved playing cuju and would not stop even in intense summer heat.
translations.idiomatic: Chang loved cuju and would play without cease even in the height of summer.

sentences.zh: 寅遜上章極諫，深被賞納。

translations.literal: Yinxun submitted a memorial strongly remonstrating and was deeply favored and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Yinxun submitted a memorial of strong remonstrance and was warmly praised and heeded.

sentences.zh: 遷新都令，拜司門郎中、知制誥、中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Magistrate of Xindu, appointed Director of the Bureau of Passes, Drafting Secretary, and Secretariat Cadet.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to magistrate of Xindu, then appointed director of the Bureau of Passes, drafting secretary, and secretariat cadet.

sentences.zh: 出知武信軍府，加史館修撰，改給事中，預修《前蜀書》，拜翰林學士，加工部侍郎，判吏部三銓事，領簡州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out to govern the Wuxin Military Commission, added Historiographical Compiler, changed to Attendant Drafting Secretary, took part in compiling the Book of Former Shu, was appointed Hanlin Academician, added Vice Minister of Works, judged the three boards of the Ministry of Personnel, and concurrently held Prefect of Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to administer the Wuxin military commission, made a historiographical compiler, then attendant drafting secretary; he helped compile the Book of Former Shu, became a Hanlin academician, was made vice minister of works and placed in charge of the Ministry of Personnel's three selection boards, and concurrently served as prefect of Jian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 隨昶歸朝，授右庶子。

translations.literal: Following Chang to surrender at court he was appointed Right Vice Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Chang to court and was made right vice mentor in the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 嚐上疏諫獵，太祖嘉之，召見賜帛。

translations.literal: He once submitted a memorial remonstrating against hunting; the Founding Emperor praised him, summoned him, and bestowed silk.
translations.idiomatic: Once he memorialized against the imperial hunt; the Founding Emperor commended him, summoned him, and gave him silk.

sentences.zh: 開寶五年，為鎮國軍行軍司馬。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaibao he was Grand Marshal of the Zhenguo Army on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Kaibao he served as grand marshal on campaign for the Zhenguo Army.

sentences.zh: 罷職，年九十餘，尚有仕進意，治裝赴闕，未登路而卒。

translations.literal: When dismissed from office he was over ninety and still had ambition to advance; he prepared his luggage to go to court but died before he set out on the road.
translations.idiomatic: After he left office he was past ninety yet still eager for further promotion; he packed to go to court but died before he could set out.

sentences.zh: 李廷珪，并州太原人。

translations.literal: Li Tinggui was a man of Taiyuan in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tinggui came from Taiyuan in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 七歲隸知祥帳下，後從入蜀。

translations.literal: At age seven he entered Zhixiang's household service; later he followed him into Shu.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he entered Zhixiang's household; later he followed him into Shu.

sentences.zh: 知祥僭號，補軍職，累遷奉鑾肅衛都虞候。

translations.literal: When Zhixiang assumed the imperial title Tinggui was given a military post and was promoted repeatedly to Deputy Commander of the Imperial Escort and Ceremonial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhixiang took the imperial title, Tinggui received a military post and rose in time to deputy commander of the Imperial Escort and Ceremonial Guard.

sentences.zh: 賞拔階州之功，領眉州刺史。

translations.literal: Rewarded for the merit of recovering Jie Prefecture, he was made concurrent Prefect of Mei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was rewarded for recovering Jie Prefecture with concurrent appointment as prefect of Mei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會圖取鳳翔，令廷珪領兵二萬出子午穀赴援。

translations.literal: When they planned to take Fengxiang, Chang ordered Tinggui to lead twenty thousand men out Ziwu Valley to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: When they plotted to take Fengxiang, Chang ordered Tinggui to lead twenty thousand men through Ziwu Valley to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 始出穀，聞趙讚為王景崇所逼，遂退軍。

translations.literal: Just as they left the valley they heard that Zhao Zan was pressed by Wang Jingchong and withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: They had barely left the valley when word came that Zhao Zan was hard pressed by Wang Jingchong, and the army turned back.

sentences.zh: 以廷珪權知興元。

translations.literal: Tinggui was appointed acting governor of Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Tinggui was made acting governor of Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 俄召歸，授捧聖控鶴都指揮使，領蜀州刺史，拜雅州永平軍節度，改右光聖都指揮使，領山南節度，改閬州保寧節度、護聖控鶴都指揮使。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled and made Commander of the Imperial Escort and Controlled Crane Forces, concurrent Prefect of Shu Prefecture, Military Commissioner of the Yongping Army at Ya Prefecture, changed to Commander of the Right Bright Sage Forces, concurrent Southern Mountains Military Commissioner, changed to Military Commissioner of the Baoning Army at Lang Prefecture and Commander of the Guardian Sage and Controlled Crane Forces.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled, made commander of the Imperial Escort and Controlled Crane Forces and concurrent prefect of Shu Prefecture, appointed military commissioner of the Yongping Army at Ya Prefecture, then commander of the Right Bright Sage Forces with concurrent southern-mountains military commission, and finally military commissioner of the Baoning Army at Lang Prefecture and commander of the Guardian Sage and Controlled Crane Forces.

sentences.zh: 周師攻秦州，以廷珪為北路行營都統。

translations.literal: When Zhou forces attacked Qin Prefecture, Tinggui was made overall commander of the northern route field army.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou troops attacked Qin Prefecture, Tinggui was named overall commander of the northern route field army.

sentences.zh: 秦、成、階三州竟為周所取，廷珪奉章待罪，昶釋之，以為左右衛聖諸軍馬步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: Qin, Cheng, and Jie prefectures were ultimately taken by Zhou; Tinggui submitted a memorial awaiting punishment, and Chang released him and made him Commander of the Horse and Foot Forces of the Left and Right Imperial Guard Armies.
translations.idiomatic: Qin, Cheng, and Jie were lost to Zhou in the end; Tinggui submitted a memorial to await punishment, but Chang pardoned him and appointed him commander of the horse and foot forces of the left and right Imperial Guard armies.

sentences.zh: 分衛聖、光聖步騎為左右十軍，以武定節度呂彥珂為之使，並隸廷珪總領之。

translations.literal: The Imperial Guard and Bright Sage foot and horse forces were divided into left and right ten armies; Military Commissioner of Wuding Lü Yanske was made their commander, all subordinate to Tinggui's overall command.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Guard and Bright Sage infantry and cavalry were split into left and right divisions of ten armies each; Lü Yanske, military commissioner of Wuding, was made their commander, all under Tinggui's overall leadership.

sentences.zh: 時論以廷珪不能救援階州，不當復總兵柄，廷珪亦自陳求解，許之。

translations.literal: Opinion held that Tinggui had failed to relieve Jie Prefecture and should not again hold military authority; Tinggui himself also submitted requesting to be relieved, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion held that Tinggui had failed to save Jie Prefecture and ought not hold command again; Tinggui himself asked to be relieved, and Chang agreed.

sentences.zh: 俄加兼侍中、蜀成都巡檢使，改遂州武信軍節度，領本鎮及保寧軍都巡檢使。

translations.literal: Soon he was further made Concurrent Palace Attendant and Chengdu inspection commissioner of Shu, changed to Military Commissioner of the Wuxin Army at Sui Prefecture, and held concurrent command of the inspection commissioner of his circuit and the Baoning Army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made concurrent palace attendant and Chengdu inspection commissioner, then military commissioner of the Wuxin Army at Sui Prefecture, holding as well the posts of inspection commissioner of his own circuit and of the Baoning Army.

sentences.zh: 王全斌之下劍關也，昶遣廷珪與其太子玄喆將兵來拒宋師，至綿、漢與全斌遇，狼狽而還。

translations.literal: When Wang Quanbin broke through Jian Pass, Chang sent Tinggui and his heir Xuanzhe to lead troops to resist the Song army; at Mian and Han they met Quanbin and fled back in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Quanbin forced Jian Pass, Chang sent Tinggui and the heir apparent Xuanzhe with an army to block the Song advance; they met Quanbin between Mian and Han and fled back in disarray.

sentences.zh: 玄喆與廷珪謀，所經州縣盡焚其儲蓄。

translations.literal: Xuanzhe and Tinggui plotted that every prefecture and county they passed through should burn all stored provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzhe and Tinggui agreed that every prefecture and county on their route should burn its stored grain.

sentences.zh: 及全斌等入成都，行營都監王仁贍案籍詰所在軍須，廷珪懼，以告馬軍都監康延澤。

translations.literal: When Quanbin and the others entered Chengdu, field-army supervisory commissioner Wang Renzan examined the registers to demand where the military supplies were; Tinggui was afraid and told Horse Forces Supervisory Commissioner Kang Yanze.
translations.idiomatic: After Quanbin entered Chengdu, field-army supervisory commissioner Wang Renzan searched the registers for military stores; Tinggui was afraid and confided in horse-forces supervisory commissioner Kang Yanze.

sentences.zh: 延澤曰：“王公誌在聲色，苟得其所欲，則置而不問矣。”

translations.literal: Yanze said: "Lord Wang's ambition lies in sound and color; if he gets what he desires he will set the matter aside and ask no more."
translations.idiomatic: Yanze said, "Lord Wang cares only for pleasure; if he gets what he wants, he will drop the matter and ask no more."

sentences.zh: 廷珪素儉約，不畜妓樂，遂求於姻戚家，得女妓四人，復假貸金帛直數百萬以遺仁贍，繇是獲免。

translations.literal: Tinggui had always been frugal and did not keep female entertainers, so he obtained four from a relative's household, and again borrowed gold and silk worth several million to present to Renzan, and thus escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Tinggui had always lived plainly and kept no singing girls; he borrowed four from a kinsman's house and took loans of gold and silk worth millions to give Renzan, and so escaped blame.

sentences.zh: 歸闕，為右千牛衛上將軍。

translations.literal: On returning to court he was made Senior General of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After he returned to court he was made senior general of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard.

sentences.zh: 乾德五年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qiande he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of Qiande.

sentences.zh: 先是，廷珪及王昭遠、韓保正川中各自有田宅，昶降後奉表上獻，詔各賜錢三百萬以償其直。

translations.literal: Earlier Tinggui and Wang Zhaoyuan and Han Baozheng each had fields and residences in the middle of Shu; after Chang surrendered they submitted memorials offering them up, and an edict granted each three million cash to compensate the value.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Tinggui, Wang Zhaoyuan, and Han Baozheng had each owned estates in central Shu; after Chang's surrender they memorialized to offer them to the throne, and an edict granted each three million cash in compensation.

sentences.zh: 李昊字穹佐，自言唐相紳之後。

translations.literal: Li Hao, style Qiongzuo, claimed descent from Tang Chancellor Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hao, courtesy name Qiongzuo, said he was descended from Tang chancellor Li Shen.

sentences.zh: 祖乾祐，建州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qianyou was Prefect of Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qianyou had been prefect of Jian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父羔，容管從事。

translations.literal: His father Gao was an aide in the Rongguan administration.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gao had served as an aide in the Rongguan administration.

sentences.zh: 昊生於關中，幼遇唐末之亂，隨父避地至奉天。

translations.literal: Hao was born in the Guanzhong region; in childhood he met the turmoil at the end of Tang and followed his father in flight to Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was born in Guanzhong; as a child he lived through the chaos at the end of Tang and fled with his father to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 值昭宗遷洛，岐軍攻破奉天，父及弟妹皆為亂兵所殺。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong moved the capital to Luoyang, Qi troops broke Fengtian, and his father and younger siblings were all killed by mutinous soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong moved the court to Luoyang, Qi troops stormed Fengtian; Hao's father and younger brothers and sisters were all killed by the mutineers.

sentences.zh: 是時年十三，獨得免，遂流寓新平十數年。

translations.literal: He was then thirteen and alone escaped; he wandered as a refugee at Xinping for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: He was thirteen and alone survived, then lived as a refugee at Xinping for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 會劉知俊領岐軍圍州城，昊逾城出，為候騎所得。

translations.literal: When Liu Zhijun led Qi troops to besiege the prefectural city, Hao climbed over the wall to get out and was seized by scouting horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zhijun led Qi forces to besiege the prefectural seat, Hao climbed over the wall to escape and was caught by scouting horsemen.

sentences.zh: 知俊與語，甚器之，置於門下，以其女妻之。

translations.literal: Zhijun spoke with him and greatly prized him, kept him in his household, and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijun talked with him, took a strong liking to him, kept him in his household, and gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 知俊歸蜀，偽署遂州武信軍節度，以昊為從事。

translations.literal: When Zhijun returned to Shu he was falsely appointed Military Commissioner of the Wuxin Army at Sui Prefecture, with Hao as aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhijun returned to Shu he was given the false title of military commissioner of the Wuxin Army at Sui Prefecture, with Hao as his aide.

sentences.zh: 王建使知俊出師，令昊主留務。

translations.literal: Wang Jian sent Zhijun on campaign and ordered Hao to oversee affairs left behind.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian sent Zhijun on campaign and left Hao in charge of affairs at home.

sentences.zh: 會建殺知俊，昊亦罷職。

translations.literal: When Jian killed Zhijun, Hao was also dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian executed Zhijun, Hao lost his post as well.

sentences.zh: 王衍襲偽位，授彭州導江令，曆中書舍人、翰林學士。

translations.literal: When Wang Yan inherited the false throne, Hao was appointed Magistrate of Daojiang in Peng Prefecture, then served as Secretariat Cadet and Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Yan took the false throne, Hao was made magistrate of Daojiang in Peng Prefecture and later served as secretariat cadet and Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 岐軍之難，昊母獨無恙。

translations.literal: In the Qi troops' disaster Hao's mother alone remained unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: In the disaster wrought by the Qi army, Hao's mother alone came through unharmed.

sentences.zh: 至是十九年，昊仕獨顯達，乃遣心膂張金、王彥間道迎其母。

translations.literal: By now nineteen years had passed; Hao alone had risen to prominence in office, and he sent trusted men Zhang Jin and Wang Yan by a secret route to welcome his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Nineteen years had now passed; Hao alone among his family had risen to high office, and he sent trusted men Zhang Jin and Wang Yan by a hidden route to bring his mother to him.

sentences.zh: 昊請告境上奉迎，衍賜以金勒名馬。

translations.literal: Hao requested leave to go to the border to meet her; Yan bestowed on him a famous horse with golden bridle.
translations.idiomatic: Hao asked leave to go to the frontier to meet her; Yan gave him a famous horse with a golden bridle.

sentences.zh: 昊至青泥嶺見母，母撫昊首號慟，哀感行路。

translations.literal: When Hao reached Qingni Ridge and saw his mother, his mother stroked Hao's head and wailed bitterly; grief moved all who passed on the road.
translations.idiomatic: At Qingni Ridge Hao met his mother; she stroked his head and wailed until travelers on the road were moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 蜀亡入洛，明宗授昊檢校兵部郎中。

translations.literal: When Shu perished he entered Luoyang; Emperor Mingzong appointed Hao Acting Vice Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu fell, Hao went to Luoyang, where Emperor Mingzong made him acting vice director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 詔西川孟知祥、三川製置使趙季良同於榷鹽、度支、戶部院間授昊一職，昊至蜀，久無所授。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Meng Zhixiang of Western Chuan and Zhao Jiliang, Commissioner for the Three Rivers Circuit, jointly to assign Hao one post among the Salt Monopoly, Revenue, and Household Affairs bureaus; Hao reached Shu but for a long time received no appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Meng Zhixiang in Western Chuan and Zhao Jiliang, commissioner for the Three Rivers circuit, to give Hao a post from among the salt monopoly, revenue, and household affairs offices; Hao reached Shu but waited a long time without any appointment.

sentences.zh: 會知祥奏季良為西川節度副使，昊辭歸洛，知祥始辟為觀風推官，遷掌書記。

translations.literal: When Zhixiang memorialized to make Jiliang Western Chuan deputy military commissioner, Hao took leave to return to Luoyang; Zhixiang then first recruited him as touring pacification staff officer and promoted him to chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhixiang had Jiliang appointed deputy military commissioner of Western Chuan, Hao resigned and returned to Luoyang; Zhixiang then took him on as a touring pacification staff officer and soon made him chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 知祥稱帝，擢為禮部侍郎、翰林學士。

translations.literal: When Zhixiang declared himself emperor, Hao was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites and Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhixiang took the imperial title, Hao was raised to vice minister of rites and Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 昶立，領漢州刺史，遷兵部侍郎，出知武德軍府，加承旨。

translations.literal: When Chang succeeded, Hao held the post of Prefect of Han Prefecture, was transferred to Vice Minister of War, went out to govern the Wude military commission, and was given the title of drafting coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang came to the throne, Hao served as prefect of Han Prefecture, then was made vice minister of war, sent out to administer the Wude military commission, and given the Hanlin drafting coordinator title.

sentences.zh: 昶嚐欲命昊二子官，昊固讓，且言：“遂州判官石欽若、蘇涯，前蜀時，同在劉知俊幕下，願回授欽若等子。”

translations.literal: Chang once wished to appoint Hao's two sons to office; Hao firmly declined and said, "The Sui Prefecture administrative aide Shi Qinruo and Su Ya, in Former Shu's day, were together with me on Liu Zhijun's staff; I wish that appointments be turned instead to Qinruo's sons and the like."
translations.idiomatic: Chang once wanted to give offices to Hao's two sons; Hao firmly refused and said, "When we were all on Liu Zhijun's staff under Former Shu, I served alongside the Sui Prefecture aides Shi Qinruo and Su Ya—let the appointments go to their sons instead."

sentences.zh: 昶嘉歎，許之，仍授昊二子官。

translations.literal: Chang praised and sighed in admiration, granted this, yet still appointed Hao's two sons to office.
translations.idiomatic: Chang admired this and agreed, but still gave offices to Hao's two sons as well.

sentences.zh: 俄加尚書左丞，拜門下侍郎兼戶部尚書、同平章事、監修國史。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Left Vice Director of the Secretariat; he was appointed Vice Director of the Chancellery concurrently Minister of Household Affairs, Associate Grand Councilor, and overseer of compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also made left vice director of the secretariat, then vice director of the chancellery, minister of household affairs, associate grand councilor, and overseer of the national history compilation.

sentences.zh: 因請置史官，乃以給事中郭廷鈞、職方員外郎趙元拱為修撰，雙流令崔崇構、成都主簿王中孚為直館。

translations.literal: Accordingly he requested establishment of historiography officials; Guo Tingjun, Attending Gentleman, and Zhao Yuangong, Outer Office Director of the Office of Military Affairs, were made compilers, and Cui Chonggou, Magistrate of Shuangliu, and Wang Zhongfu, Registrar of Chengdu, were made duty archivists.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that historiography posts be created, and Guo Tingjun, an attending gentleman, and Zhao Yuangong, an outer-office director in the office of military affairs, were named compilers; Cui Chonggou, magistrate of Shuangliu, and Wang Zhongfu, registrar of Chengdu, were made duty archivists.

sentences.zh: 俄加昊左仆射。

translations.literal: Soon Hao was further made Left Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Hao was also made left grandee.

sentences.zh: 昶令就知祥真容院圖文武三品以上於東西廊，以昊有參佐功，特畫於殿內。

translations.literal: Chang ordered that in Zhixiang's portrait hall civil and military officials of the third rank and above be painted in the east and west corridors; because Hao had merit as adviser and aide, his portrait was specially painted inside the main hall.
translations.idiomatic: Chang ordered portraits of all civil and military officials of the third rank and above painted in the east and west corridors of Zhixiang's portrait hall; because Hao had long served as his adviser, Hao's portrait was placed inside the main hall.

sentences.zh: 自知祥領蜀，凡章奏書檄皆出昊手，至是集為百卷曰《經緯略》以獻，昶齎以珍器、錦彩。

translations.literal: From the time Zhixiang held Shu, every memorial, letter, and proclamation had come from Hao's hand; now these were collected in a hundred fascicles called Jingwei Lue and presented; Chang rewarded him with precious vessels and brocades.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since Zhixiang had held Shu, every memorial, dispatch, and proclamation had come from Hao's pen; he now gathered them in a hundred fascicles titled Overview of Statecraft and presented them; Chang rewarded him with precious vessels and brocades.

sentences.zh: 俄命判度支戶部。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to administer the Revenue and Household Affairs bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was put in charge of revenue and household affairs.

sentences.zh: 廣政十四年，修成昶《實錄》四十卷。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Guangzheng, he completed Chang's Veritable Records in forty fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Guangzheng he finished the Veritable Records of Chang in forty fascicles.

sentences.zh: 昶欲取觀，昊曰：“帝王不閱史，不敢奉詔。”

translations.literal: Chang wished to examine them; Hao said, "Sovereigns do not read the histories—I dare not obey the edict."
translations.idiomatic: Chang wanted to read them; Hao said, "Emperors do not peruse the histories—I cannot comply with such an order."

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，裁百日，起復。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother; only a hundred days had passed when he was recalled to office.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he went into mourning, but after only a hundred days he was recalled to office.

sentences.zh: 俄修《前蜀書》，命昊與趙元拱、王中孚及左諫議大夫喬諷、給事中馮侃、知制誥賈玄珪幸寅遜、太府少卿郭微、右司郎中黃彬同撰，成四十卷上之。

translations.literal: Soon they compiled the Book of Former Shu, ordering Hao together with Zhao Yuangong, Wang Zhongfu, Left Remonstrance Counselor Qiao Feng, Attending Gentleman Feng Kan, Drafting Drafter Jia Xuangui, Xing Yinxun, Vice Director of the Palace Commissariat Guo Wei, and Director of the Right Office Huang Bin to compose jointly; when forty fascicles were finished they were submitted.
translations.idiomatic: They soon began the Book of Former Shu, with Hao, Zhao Yuangong, Wang Zhongfu, remonstrance counselor Qiao Feng, attending gentleman Feng Kan, drafting drafter Jia Xuangui, Xing Yinxun, vice director of the palace commissariat Guo Wei, and right-office director Huang Bin as co-authors; when forty fascicles were complete they submitted them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 以判使辦集，封趙國公。

translations.literal: For his service as chief commissioner in securing provisions he was enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: For his success as chief commissioner in gathering supplies he was enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 俄加司空，領遂州武信軍節度，出判鹽鐵，加弘文館大學士，修奉太廟禮儀使。

translations.literal: Soon he was further made Minister of Works, concurrently held the military commission of the Wuxin Army at Sui Prefecture, went out to administer salt and iron, was made Grand Academician of the Hongwen Hall, and made Commissioner for Rites in Serving the Imperial Ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon also made minister of works and military commissioner of the Wuxin Army at Sui Prefecture, put in charge of salt and iron, made grand academician of the Hongwen Hall, and appointed commissioner for ancestral temple rites.

sentences.zh: 昶嚐召四孫，悉授太子司儀郎舍人，並賜緋。

translations.literal: Chang once summoned his four grandsons, all appointed Gentlemen-in-Attendance of the Crown Prince's Ceremonial Office and Drafting Attendants, and each given crimson robes.
translations.idiomatic: Chang once summoned all four grandsons, made each of them a gentleman-in-attendance in the crown prince's ceremonial office and drafting attendant, and gave them crimson robes.

sentences.zh: 昊又改判度支使。

translations.literal: Hao was again transferred to administer the Revenue Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was again placed in charge of the revenue commission.

sentences.zh: 其子孝連尚昶女鳳儀公主，累遷太常少卿、資州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Xiaolian married Chang's daughter Princess Fengyi; he rose through posts to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Prefect of Zi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaolian had married Chang's daughter, Princess Fengyi, and rose to vice director of the court of imperial sacrifices and prefect of Zi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 長子孝逢，給事中。

translations.literal: The eldest son Xiaofeng was Attending Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Xiaofeng served as an attending gentleman.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，隨昶入朝，太祖優待之，拜昊工部尚書，賜第。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified he followed Chang to court; Taizu treated him generously, appointed Hao Minister of Works, and granted him a residence.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu was conquered, he followed Chang to the Song court; Emperor Taizu treated him generously, made him minister of works, and granted him a mansion.

sentences.zh: 以孝逢為膳部郎中，孝連為將作少監。

translations.literal: Xiaofeng was made Director in the Bureau of Provisions, Xiaolian Vice Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaofeng was made a director in the bureau of provisions, and Xiaolian vice director of the directorate of palace buildings.

sentences.zh: 親屬乘舟自峽下，至夷陵，妻死，昊聞，悲愴成疾而卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: Relatives came down the gorges by boat; reaching Yiling, his wife died; when Hao heard this he fell ill from grief and died, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: Relatives were traveling downriver from the gorges; at Yiling his wife died, and when Hao heard the news grief brought on illness and he died, aged seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 贈右仆射。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title of Right Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made right grandee.

sentences.zh: 昊前後仕蜀五十年。

translations.literal: Hao had served Shu for fifty years in all.
translations.idiomatic: Hao had served in Shu for fifty years altogether.

sentences.zh: 昶之世，位兼將相，秉利權，資貨歲入钜萬，奢侈尤甚，後堂妓妾曳羅綺數百人。

translations.literal: In Chang's reign he held ranks of both general and minister, wielded profit power, and his yearly income in goods ran to tens of thousands; his extravagance was extreme, with several hundred singing girls and concubines in trailing silk and brocade in the rear hall.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chang he held both civil and military rank, controlled lucrative offices, and took in tens of thousands in goods each year; his extravagance was extreme—several hundred singing girls and concubines in trailing silks filled his rear hall.

sentences.zh: 昶與江南李景通好，遣其臣趙季劄至江南，購得李紳武宗朝入相制書，還以遺昊。

translations.literal: Chang was on friendly terms with Li Jing of Jiangnan and sent his minister Zhao Jizha to Jiangnan, where he purchased Li Shen's appointment commission when he entered the chancellery in Emperor Wuzong's reign, and on returning presented it to Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was on friendly terms with Li Jing of the south and sent his minister Zhao Jizha to Jiangnan to buy Li Shen's appointment edict from his entry into the chancellorship under Emperor Wuzong; on his return he gave it to Hao.

sentences.zh: 昊結彩樓置其中，盡召成都聲妓，昊朝服前迎歸私第，大會賓客宴飲，所費無算。

translations.literal: Hao erected a decorated pavilion and placed it within; he summoned all of Chengdu's singing girls; in court dress Hao went forward to welcome it to his private residence and held a great banquet for guests with feasting—the cost beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Hao built a decorated pavilion to house it, summoned every singing girl in Chengdu, went out in court dress to welcome the document to his home, and threw a banquet for guests at incalculable expense.

sentences.zh: 以帛二千匹謝季劄。

translations.literal: He presented two thousand bolts of silk to Jizha in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Zhao Jizha two thousand bolts of silk in thanks.

sentences.zh: 初，王衍降莊宗，昊草其表；

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wang Yan surrendered to Emperor Zhuangzong, Hao had drafted his memorial;
translations.idiomatic: Years earlier, when Wang Yan surrendered to Emperor Zhuangzong, Hao had drafted his memorial of surrender;

sentences.zh: 昶之降也，其表亦昊所為。

translations.literal: when Chang surrendered; that memorial too was Hao's work.
translations.idiomatic: when Chang surrendered, that memorial too was Hao's work.

sentences.zh: 蜀人潛署其門曰“世修降表李家”，見者哂之。

translations.literal: People of Shu secretly posted at his gate, "The Li family—hereditary authors of surrender memorials"; those who saw it snickered.
translations.idiomatic: Someone in Shu secretly posted on his gate, "The Li family, hereditary drafters of surrender memorials," and passersby laughed.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷，目為《樞機應用集》。

translations.literal: He had a collected writings in twenty fascicles, entitled Applied Anthology of State Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collection in twenty fascicles titled Applied Writings from the Inner Circle.

sentences.zh: 孝連後至司農少卿。

translations.literal: Xiaolian later reached the post of Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaolian later rose to vice director of the court of the imperial granaries.

sentences.zh: 昊孫德鏻至國子博士，德錞進士及第。

translations.literal: Hao's grandson Delin became Erudite of the Directorate of Education; Dekun passed the presented-scholar examination.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's grandson Delin became an erudite of the directorate of education; Dekun passed the civil service examination.

sentences.zh: 毋守素字表淳，河中龍門人。

translations.literal: Wu Shousu, style Biaochun, was a native of Longmen in Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shousu, courtesy name Biaochun, was from Longmen in Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 父昭裔，偽蜀宰相、太子太師致仕。

translations.literal: His father Zhaoyi was chief councilor of false Shu and retired as Grandee Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhaoyi had been chief councilor of Former Shu and retired as grandee tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 守素弱冠起家，偽授秘書郎，累遷戶部員外郎、知制誥，真拜中書舍人、工部侍郎，出為雲安榷鹽使。

translations.literal: Shousu began his career at the capping age; falsely appointed Secretary; he rose through Household Affairs Outer Office Director and Drafting Drafter to formal appointment as Secretariat Cadet and Vice Minister of Works, then went out as Yun'an Salt Monopoly Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Shousu entered government in his youth; under the Shu regime he was made a secretary, rose through posts in the household ministry and as drafting drafter, was formally appointed secretariat cadet and vice minister of works, and then sent out as salt monopoly commissioner at Yun'an.

sentences.zh: 召見其二子克溫、克恭，並賜緋；

translations.literal: He was summoned with his two sons Kewen and Kegong; both were granted crimson robes;
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned along with his two sons Kewen and Kegong, and both were given crimson robes;

sentences.zh: 以次子克恭尚昶女，授檢校水部員外郎。

translations.literal: his younger son Kegong had married Chang's daughter and was appointed Acting Outer Office Director in the Ministry of Works' Water Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: his younger son Kegong, who had married one of Chang's daughters, was made acting outer-office director in the water bureau.

sentences.zh: 廣政二十年，拜工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Guangzheng he was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Guangzheng he was made minister of works.

sentences.zh: 時昭裔判鹽鐵，衰老不能親職，委其務於判官李光遠，事多留滯。

translations.literal: At the time Zhaoyi administered salt and iron; aged and unable to attend to duties in person, he entrusted affairs to administrative aide Li Guangyuan, and many matters stalled.
translations.idiomatic: At the time his father Zhaoyi oversaw salt and iron but was too old to handle the work himself; he delegated affairs to aide Li Guangyuan, and business piled up.

sentences.zh: 昶患之，命守素代判使務。

translations.literal: Chang was troubled by this and ordered Shousu to replace him in administering the commissioner's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was concerned and ordered Shousu to take over the commissioner's duties.

sentences.zh: 父子相代，時頗榮之。

translations.literal: Father and son succeeded each other; at the time this was much admired.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son holding the post in succession was seen at the time as a notable honor.

sentences.zh: 俄改判度支，領彭州刺史，又判鹽鐵。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to administer revenue, concurrently held the prefecture of Peng, and again administered salt and iron.
translations.idiomatic: He soon shifted to revenue administration while serving as prefect of Peng Prefecture, and later took charge of salt and iron again.

sentences.zh: 守素奉親頗勤至，雖隆暑暮歸，必朝服執簡以申昏定之禮。

translations.literal: Shousu was quite dutiful in serving his parents; even in blazing summer when he returned at dusk he always wore court robes and held his tally board to perform the evening comfort rite.
translations.idiomatic: Shousu was remarkably dutiful toward his parents; even on sweltering summer evenings when he came home at dusk he would put on court dress and carry his tally board to perform the evening obeisance.

sentences.zh: 蜀亡入朝，授工部侍郎，籍其蜀中莊產茶園以獻，詔賜錢三百萬以充其直，仍賜第於京城。

translations.literal: When Shu fell and he entered court he was appointed Vice Minister of Works; he registered his estates and tea plantations in Shu and presented them; an edict granted three million cash to make up their value, and he was still granted a residence in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu fell he entered Song service as vice minister of works; he registered his estates and tea plantations in Shu and offered them to the throne; the court paid him three million cash as compensation and granted him a mansion in the capital.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，為兄之子岳州司法正己訟其居父喪娶妾免，正己亦坐奪一官。

translations.literal: After more than a year his elder brother's son Zhengji, a judicial official at Yue Prefecture, sued him for taking a concubine while in mourning for his father and he was dismissed; Zhengji also suffered demotion by one rank.
translations.idiomatic: A year later his nephew Zhengji, a judicial officer in Yue Prefecture, sued him for taking a concubine during his father's mourning period and he was dismissed; Zhengji was also demoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 開寶初，起為國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Early in Kaibao he was recalled as Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaibao era he was recalled as chancellor of the directorate of education.

sentences.zh: 太祖征河東，命權知趙州。

translations.literal: When Taizu campaigned against Hedong he was ordered to act as prefect of Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu campaigned in Hedong, he was made acting prefect of Zhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及平嶺表，移知容州，兼本管諸州水陸轉運使。

translations.literal: When Lingbiao was pacified he was transferred to govern Rong Prefecture and concurrently made Commissioner for Water-and-Land Transport of all prefectures in the circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After the Lingnan region was pacified he was made prefect of Rong Prefecture and concurrently commissioner for water and land transport in his circuit.

sentences.zh: 先是，部民有逋賦者，或縣吏代輸，或於兼並之家假貸，則皆納其妻女以為質。

translations.literal: Previously, among the people of his jurisdiction there were those who owed back taxes; sometimes county clerks paid on their behalf, sometimes they borrowed from encroaching magnate households—in every case their wives and daughters were taken as pledge.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, taxpayers in arrears might have county clerks pay for them or borrow from powerful local lenders—and in every such case their wives and daughters were taken as collateral.

sentences.zh: 守素表其事，即日降詔禁止。

translations.literal: Shousu memorialized on this; that very day an edict was issued forbidding the practice.
translations.idiomatic: Shousu reported this to the throne, and the very same day an edict banned the practice.

sentences.zh: 六年，卒，年五十三。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died, aged fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of Kaibao, aged fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 昭裔性好藏書，在成都令門人勾中正、孫逢吉書《文選》、《初學記》、《白氏六帖》鏤板，守素齎至中朝，行於世。

translations.literal: Zhaoyi was fond of collecting books; in Chengdu he had his disciples Gou Zhongzheng and Sun Fengji write out the Wenxuan, Chuxueji, and Bai's Six Tablets for printing blocks; Shousu brought these to the central court and they circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyi loved books; in Chengdu he had his students Gou Zhongzheng and Sun Fengji prepare woodblocks for the Wenxuan, the Chuxueji, and Bai Juyi's Six Tablets; Shousu brought the blocks to the Song court, where they were printed and widely circulated.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符九年，子克勤上其板，補三班奉職。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Dazhong Xiangfu his son Keqin presented the blocks and was given a supplementary post as Third-Rank Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Dazhong Xiangfu his son Keqin presented the blocks and was given a supplemental third-rank attendant post.

sentences.zh: 次子克恭，尚昶女鑾國公主，仕為光祿少卿，歸宋，至左監門衛將軍。

translations.literal: The younger son Kegong had married Chang's daughter Princess Chuanguo; in office he was Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; after submitting to Song he rose to General of the Left Palace Gate Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His younger son Kegong had married Chang's daughter, Princess Chuanguo; under Shu he rose to vice director of the court of imperial entertainments, and after submitting to Song he became a general of the left palace gate guard.

sentences.zh: 歐陽迥，益州華陽人。

translations.literal: Ouyang Jiong was a native of Huayang in Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Jiong was from Huayang in Yi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父玨，通泉令。

translations.literal: His father Jue was Magistrate of Tongquan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jue had been magistrate of Tongquan.

sentences.zh: 迥少事王衍，為中書舍人。

translations.literal: Jiong in youth served Wang Yan as Secretariat Cadet.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Jiong served Wang Yan and was made a secretariat cadet.

sentences.zh: 後唐同光中，蜀平，隨衍至洛陽，補秦州從事。

translations.literal: In the Tongguang era of Later Tang, when Shu was pacified, he followed Yan to Luoyang and was appointed aide at Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tongguang era of Later Tang, when Shu fell, he followed Yan to Luoyang and was made an administrative aide in Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 知祥鎮成都，迥復來入蜀。

translations.literal: When Zhixiang held Chengdu as his garrison, Jiong returned and entered Shu again.
translations.idiomatic: When Meng Zhixiang was posted at Chengdu, Jiong returned to Shu.

sentences.zh: 知祥僭號，以為中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Zhixiang usurped the title he was made Secretariat Cadet.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhixiang took the imperial title, Jiong was made secretariat cadet.

sentences.zh: 廣政十二年，拜翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Guangzheng he was appointed Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Guangzheng he was made a Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 明年，知貢舉、判太常寺。

translations.literal: The next year he supervised the civil examinations and administered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he supervised the civil examinations and headed the court of imperial sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部侍郎，領陵州刺史，轉吏部侍郎，加承旨。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites, concurrently Prefect of Ling Prefecture, then transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel, and given the drafting coordinator title.
