translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of rites and prefect of Ling Prefecture, then to vice minister of personnel with the Hanlin drafting coordinator title.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，拜門下侍郎兼戶部尚書、平章事、監修國史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was appointed Vice Director of the Chancellery concurrently Minister of Household Affairs, Grand Councilor, and overseer of compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of Guangzheng he was made vice director of the chancellery, minister of household affairs, grand councilor, and overseer of the national history.

sentences.zh: 嚐擬白居易諷諫詩五十篇以獻，昶手詔嘉美，賚以銀器、錦彩。

translations.literal: He once composed fifty admonitory poems in the style of Bai Juyi and presented them; Chang personally praised them in an edict and rewarded him with silver vessels and brocades.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote fifty admonitory poems in Bai Juyi's manner and presented them to Chang, who praised them in a personal edict and rewarded him with silver vessels and brocades.

sentences.zh: 從昶歸朝，為右散騎常侍，俄充翰林學士，就轉左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Following Chang to court he was made Right Regular Attendant of Fast Cavalry, soon served as Hanlin Academician, and was then transferred to Left Regular Attendant of Fast Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Chang to the Song court as right attendant of the fast cavalry, soon became a Hanlin academician, and was then promoted to left attendant of the fast cavalry.

sentences.zh: 嶺南平，議遣迥祭南海，迥聞之稱病不出。

translations.literal: When Lingnan was pacified it was proposed to send Jiong to sacrifice to the Southern Sea; on hearing this he claimed illness and did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: After Lingnan was pacified the court proposed sending Jiong to perform rites to the Southern Sea; when he heard of it he claimed illness and stayed home.

sentences.zh: 太祖怒，罷其職，以本官分司西京。

translations.literal: Taizu was angry, removed him from office, and kept him at his original rank on detached service in the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was furious, stripped him of office, and kept him at his former rank on detached duty in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 開寶四年，卒，年七十六。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaibao he died, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Kaibao, aged seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title of Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made minister of works.

sentences.zh: 迥性坦率，無檢操，雅善長笛。

translations.literal: Jiong's nature was frank and open, without restraint in conduct; he was skilled at playing the long flute.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong was frank and unrestrained, and was an accomplished player of the long flute.

sentences.zh: 太祖常召於偏殿，令奏數曲。

translations.literal: Taizu often summoned him to a side hall and ordered him to perform several tunes.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu often summoned him to a side hall and had him play several pieces.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞劉溫叟聞之，叩殿門求見，諫曰：“禁署之職，典司誥命，不可作伶人之事。”

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Wensou heard of this, knocked at the palace gate and asked audience, and remonstrated, "The posts of the forbidden precincts are charged with managing imperial mandates—it is not fitting to do the work of entertainers."
translations.idiomatic: Vice censor-in-chief Liu Wensou heard of this, knocked at the palace gate for an audience, and remonstrated: "Officials of the forbidden precinct handle imperial edicts—they should not perform like entertainers."

sentences.zh: 上曰：“朕嚐聞孟昶君臣溺於聲樂，迥至宰司尚習此技，故為我所擒。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I have heard that Meng Chang and his ministers were drowned in music; Jiong, though reaching the rank of chief minister, still practices this art—that is why he fell into my hands."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I had heard that Meng Chang and his court were lost to music and song; Jiong rose to chief minister yet still practiced this art—that is why he fell to us."

sentences.zh: 所以召迥，欲驗言者之不誣也。”

translations.literal: The reason I summoned Jiong was to verify that those who spoke had not lied.
translations.idiomatic: I summoned Jiong only to see whether what people said was true.

sentences.zh: 溫叟謝曰：“臣愚不識陛下鑒戒之微旨。”

translations.literal: Wensou apologized and said, "Your servant is foolish and did not understand Your Majesty's subtle purpose in taking this as a warning."
translations.idiomatic: Wensou apologized: "I was too dull to grasp Your Majesty's deeper purpose in this lesson."

sentences.zh: 自是不復召。

translations.literal: From then on Jiong was no longer summoned.
translations.idiomatic: After that he was never summoned again.

sentences.zh: 迥好為歌詩，雖多而不工，掌誥命亦非所長。

translations.literal: Jiong liked to write songs and poems; though he wrote many they were not well crafted, and drafting mandates too was not his strong point.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong enjoyed writing verse, but though prolific he was not skilled at it, and drafting imperial edicts was not his strength either.

sentences.zh: 但在蜀日，卿相以奢靡相尚，迥猶能守儉素，此其可稱也。

translations.literal: Yet in his days in Shu, when ministers and councilors vied in extravagance, Jiong could still keep to frugal simplicity—this is worth praise.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in Shu, when ministers and councilors competed in extravagance, Jiong still lived plainly—and that is something to his credit.
